Raji was selected in the first round with the ninth overall pick by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the [[2009 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/draft.htm |access-date=May 12, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was worked into defensive coordinator [[Dom Capers]]' brand new [[3–4 defense|3–4 scheme]] during the start of the Packers 2009 season. Raji held out during the 2009 training camp and completed his deal on August 14. Hampered by an ankle injury for the entire season, he appeared in fourteen games (once as a starter), and managed 25 tackles and 1 sack.

Fully recovered and expected to fully contribute for the 2010 season, Raji earned the starting position at the sole defensive tackle position in Capers' 3–4 type defense, switching previous starter [[Ryan Pickett]] to defensive end. 2010 was a breakout season, as he started in all 16 games. Raji became the defensive anchor that the Packers had envisioned, accumulating 39 tackles with 6.5 sacks, along with 3 passes defended.

The Packers began using Raji as an additional fullback in their goal line offense during the 2011 postseason, which led to Raji nicknaming himself "the Freezer" in homage to [[William Perry (American football)|William Perry]], who played for the Bears and was nicknamed "the Fridge".<ref name="B.J. Raji dancing his way to stardom">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/36462|title=XLV: B.J. Raji dancing his way to stardom|date=January 25, 2011|website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/story/14600283/freezer-raji-lobbies-to-carry-the-rock-in-super-bowl/cbsnews|title=Freezer Raji lobbies to carry the rock in Super Bowl}}</ref> On January 23, 2011, in the fourth quarter of the [[2010 NFC Championship Game]] at [[Soldier Field]] in [[Chicago]], Raji intercepted a pass from Bears backup quarterback [[Caleb Hanie]] and returned it 18 yards to the end zone, marking Raji's first career [[interception]] and touchdown.<ref name="B.J. Raji dancing his way to stardom"/> The 337-pound Raji performed a memorable [[hula dance]] after the touchdown, an incident that was parodied in a [[State Farm Insurance]] commercial featuring Raji and [[Aaron Rodgers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RxYJb2ScuXM|title=YouTube|website=www.youtube.com}}</ref> The play also broke [[William Perry (American football)|William Perry]]'s NFL record for the heaviest player to score a post-season touchdown.<ref name="B.J. Raji dancing his way to stardom"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052748703555804576102254210696910|title=Raji Knocks Fridge From His Perch|newspaper=Wall Street Journal |date=January 25, 2011|via=www.wsj.com}}</ref> The touchdown proved to be the decisive score, and with that interception, the Packers advanced to [[Super Bowl XLV]], where they defeated the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] by a score of 31–25.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201102060pit.htm |title=Super Bowl XLV - Pittsburgh Steelers vs. Green Bay Packers - February 6th, 2011 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=December 15, 2017}}</ref> He was ranked 81st by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2011]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2011-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=March 18, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

[[File:B.J. Raji.jpg|thumb|Raji against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in 2011]]

In early August 2011, Raji was named the co-host of the "In The Huddle" radio show along with longtime Wisconsin sports reporter Bill Scott. The one-hour show airs live from Tanner's Sports Bar in [[Kimberly, Wisconsin|Kimberly]] near Green Bay.

During a Week 11 matchup against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] on November 20, on his first and only carry of his career, Raji scored a rushing touchdown in the 35–26 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201111200gnb.htm |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Green Bay Packers - November 20th, 2011 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=August 10, 2018}}</ref> He was only the fourth defensive lineman to score a rushing touchdown since the NFL/[[American Football League|AFL]] merger.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=311120009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820204618/http://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=311120009|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 20, 2016|title=Buccaneers vs. Packers - Game Recap - November 20, 2011 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> On December 28, 2011, he was elected to his first [[Pro Bowl]] appearance. In 16 games of the 2011 season, Raji registered 3 sacks and 2 passes defended on 24 tackles. The Packers finished the season with an NFL-best 15–1 record for an [[NFC North]] pennant, but lost to the [[New York Giants]] 37–20 in the divisional round.

[[File:2012 Packers vs Giants - B. J. Raji.jpg|right|thumb|190px|Raji against the [[New York Giants]] in January 2012]]
Raji played in 14 games in the 2012 season, making 26 tackles and defended two passes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=B.J. Raji 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RajiBJ99/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=2024-11-05 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

The Packers' defensive line became short-handed in 2013 due to injuries. Raji was transitioned to defensive end, while Ryan Pickett maintained the role at defensive tackle. He started all 16 games at defensive end, making 17 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=B.J. Raji 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RajiBJ99/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=2024-11-05 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On August 22, 2014, in a [[preseason]] game against the [[Oakland Raiders]], Raji suffered a torn right [[biceps]]. He was subsequently placed on [[injured reserve]], and missed the entire [[2014 NFL season]].<ref name="i854">{{cite web | last=Patra | first=Kevin | title=B.J. Raji tears biceps, will miss Packers' season | website=NFL.com | date=2014-08-23 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/b-j-raji-tears-biceps-will-miss-packers-season-0ap3000000382312 | access-date=2025-01-06}}</ref>

On March 30, 2015, Raji signed a one-year, $3.5 million deal with the Packers.<ref name="r175">{{cite web | title=B.J. Raji returning to Packers on one-year deal | website=NFL.com | date=2015-03-30 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/b-j-raji-returning-to-packers-on-one-year-deal-0ap3000000482484 | access-date=2024-11-05}}</ref> In the [[2015 NFL season|2015 season]], Raji totaled 22 tackles and half a sack.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Welk|first1=Sam|title=2015 Packers Position Grades: Defense and Special Teams|url=https://sconniesportstalk.com/2016/01/20/2015-packers-position-grades-defense-and-special-teams/|website=Sconnie Sports Talk|date=January 20, 2016}}</ref>

===Retirement and possible return===
On March 14, 2016, Raji announced his retirement from professional football after seven seasons, but noted he planned on returning to the league and that he was simply taking a "hiatus".<ref name="d383">{{cite web | last=Sessler | first=Marc | title=B.J. Raji to take hiatus from NFL after seven seasons | website=NFL.com | date=2016-03-14 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/b-j-raji-to-take-hiatus-from-nfl-after-seven-seasons-0ap3000000644234 | access-date=2024-07-24}}</ref> However, as of 2026, he has remained retired.

'''Auston English''' (born March 10, 1987) is a former [[American football]] [[defensive end]].

On April 30, 2010, English was signed as an undrafted [[free agent]] by the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-sign-10-free-agents/2ac213be-f82c-4a49-86e6-547209798a57 |title=Browns sign 10 free agents |publisher=Clevelandbrowns.com |accessdate=May 1, 2010 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100502003855/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-sign-10-free-agents/2ac213be-f82c-4a49-86e6-547209798a57 |archivedate=May 2, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On September 4, 2011, English was waived by the Cleveland Browns.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dawgsbynature.com/2011/9/4/2404826/browns-waive-ben-jacobs-auston-english-and-derreck-robinson-practice|title=Browns Waive Ben Jacobs, Auston English, and Derreck Robinson; Practice Squad Announced|publisher=dawgsbynature.com|date=September 4, 2011|accessdate=September 5, 2011}}</ref> On September 5, 2011, he was signed to the Browns' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.woio.com/story/15397772/browns-add-two-to-practice-squad|title=Browns add two to practice squad|publisher=woio.com|date=September 5, 2011|accessdate=September 6, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120328030538/http://www.woio.com/story/15397772/browns-add-two-to-practice-squad|archive-date=March 28, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On August 3, 2013, English was signed by the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]]. In 4 games with the Argonauts, English recorded 8 tackles.  English was released by the Argonauts on October 27, 2013.

'''Bryan Cunningham, Jr.'''<ref name="msuspartans.com">{{cite web|url=http://msuspartans.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2161|title=B.J. Cunningham - Football|website=Michigan State University Athletics}}</ref> (born May 29, 1989) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State Spartans]]. He was selected in the sixth round at the 183rd overall pick in the [[2012 NFL draft]] by the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref name=Zurkowsky>{{cite news|last1=Zurkowsky|first1=Herb|title=B.J. Cunningham grateful to Alouettes for giving him a chance to excel|url=https://nationalpost.com/sports/football/cfl/montreal-alouettes/b-j-cunningham-grateful-to-alouettes-for-giving-him-a-chance-to-excel|access-date=9 August 2017|work=National Post|date=9 August 2017}}</ref> He was also a member of the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], [[Chicago Bears]], [[Montreal Alouettes]] and [[Ottawa Redblacks]].

==Early life==
Cunningham attended [[Westerville South High School]] in [[Westerville, Ohio]]. As a senior, he had 45 receptions for 770 yards and nine [[touchdowns]].

==College career==
Cunningham concluded his career at Michigan State as the school's all-time leader in receptions (218) and receiving yards (3,086). He also ranks second in career TD receptions with 25.<ref name="msuspartans.com"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://bostonherald.com/sports/college/football/view.bg?articleid=1385840&srvc=home&position=active|title=A Spartans' heartbreaker: Wisconsin's late rally destroys MSU's Rose Bowl dream|publisher=}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Miami Dolphins===
He was selected in the sixth round of the [[2012 NFL draft]] by the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On May 17 of that year, Cunningham signed a four-year $2.2 million contract; includes a $106,000 signing bonus. Cunningham was, however, cut by the Dolphins on August 31, 2012.<ref name=Zurkowsky/>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
Cunningham was signed to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] practice squad on September 1, 2012. On August 1, 2013, Cunningham was waived with an injury settlement by the Philadelphia Eagles.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Eagles-Waive-WR-BJ-Cunningham/dce50981-49b1-40a4-973e-a49ba1dad29b |title=Eagles Waive WR B.J. Cunningham |date=August 1, 2013 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |access-date=August 2, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130805195228/http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Eagles-Waive-WR-BJ-Cunningham/dce50981-49b1-40a4-973e-a49ba1dad29b |archive-date=August 5, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On October 14, 2013, Cunningham was re-signed to the Eagles' active roster. He was released on November 12, 2013. Two days later, he was signed to Eagles' [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web|work=CSNPhilly.com |url=http://www.csnphilly.com/football-philadelphia-eagles/eagles-re-sign-bj-cunningham-prax-squad |title=Eagles re-sign B.J. Cunningham to prax squad |first=Geoff |last=Mosher |date=November 14, 2013 |access-date=2014-04-19 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131115143344/http://www.csnphilly.com/football-philadelphia-eagles/eagles-re-sign-bj-cunningham-prax-squad |archive-date=2013-11-15 }}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
Cunningham was signed to the [[Chicago Bears]] practice squad on November 12, 2014.

===Montreal Alouettes===
Cunningham was signed by the [[Montreal Alouettes]] on July 28, 2015. After a modest [[2015 CFL season|2015 season]] Cunningham had a breakout [[2016 CFL season|2016 campaign]], playing in 17 regular season games catching 65 passes for 855 yards with 4 touchdowns.<ref name=Zurkowsky/> The following season, in 2017, he had the best season of his career, catching 69 passes for 1,128 yards with 4 touchdowns. Cunningham missed four games in the [[2018 CFL season|2018 season]] but was still a significant contributor to the Alouettes' passing attack.  In February 2019, Cunningham signed a contract extension with Montreal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2019/02/12/als-extended-cunningham-2020/|title=Als extended Cunningham through 2020|date=12 February 2019|publisher=}}</ref> In August 2019, Cunningham suffered a fractured wrist and played in just six games.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tsn.ca/report-montreal-alouettes-wr-b-j-cunningham-suffers-fractured-wrist-1.1349465|title=Report: Montreal Alouettes WR B.J. Cunningham suffers fractured wrist - TSN.ca|author=TSN ca Staff|date=2019-08-10|website=TSN|language=en|access-date=2019-08-12}}</ref> He signed a one-year contract extension with the Alouettes on January 25, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Receiver B.J. Cunningham remains with the Alouettes |url=https://en.montrealalouettes.com/2021/01/25/receiver-b-j-cunningham-remains-alouettes/ |website=MontrealAlouettes.com |date=January 25, 2021 |access-date=February 22, 2021}}</ref> For the [[2021 Montreal Alouettes season|2021 season]], Cunningham played in nine games where he had 36 receptions for 474 yards and one touchdown. He became a free agent upon the expiry of his contract on February 8, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/2022/ |title=Transactions – Football player trades and signings |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 12, 2022}}</ref>

===Ottawa Redblacks===
On February 10, 2022, it was announced that Cunningham had signed with the [[Ottawa Redblacks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ottawaredblacks.com/2022/02/10/redblacks-add-free-agent-receiver-b-j-cunningham/ |title=Redblacks add free agent receiver B. J. Cunningham |publisher=[[Ottawa Redblacks]] |date=February 10, 2022}}</ref> Cunningham was released as part of the team's final roster cuts on June 4, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-05 |title=REDBLACKS set roster for 2022 season opener |url=https://www.ottawaredblacks.com/2022/06/04/redblacks-set-roster-for-2022-season-opener/ |access-date=2022-06-06 |website=Ottawa REDBLACKS |language=en}}</ref>

He was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the seventh round of the [[2012 NFL draft]]. ==Early life== Bryon Elwyn Coleman Jr. was born on September 16, 1988. He played [[high school football]] at [[The McCallie School]] in Chattanooga. He passed for 1,993 yards and 15 touchdowns his sophomore year in 2004 and 2,203 yards and 19 touchdowns as a junior in 2005. In the class of 2007, he was rated the No. 10 pro-style quarterback by [[Rivals.com]], the No. 16 overall quarterback by [[Scout.com]], and the No. 90 overall quarterback by [[ESPN.com]]. Coleman was also a three-year starter on the [[baseball]] team in high school, playing both [[pitcher]] and [[Outfielder|outfield]]. == College career == Coleman first played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee Volunteers]] of the [[University of Tennessee]]. He was [[redshirted]] in 2007. He played in three games in 2008, completing four of eight passes for 21 yards and one interception.{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bj-coleman-1.html | title=B.J. He missed part of the 2011 season due to a shoulder injury on his throwing arm. His 6,871 career passing yards were the second most in school history. Coleman was invited to the [[East–West Shrine Game]] after his senior year. ''' William Wilson''' "'''B. W.'''" '''Webb Jr.''' (born May 3, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[William & Mary Tribe football|William & Mary Tribe]], and was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the fourth round of the [[2013 NFL draft]]. He was also a member of the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], [[New York Giants]], [[Cleveland Browns]], [[Chicago Bears]], [[New Orleans Saints]], [[Tennessee Titans]], [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], [[Arizona Cardinals]], and [[San Francisco 49ers]].

==Early life==
Webb was born in [[Newport News, Virginia]].  He attended [[Warwick High School (Newport News)|Warwick High School]] and [[Hampton Roads Academy]] under the tutelage of Coach Abe Mikell in Newport News, and played high school football for the Warwick Raiders.  While working with Coach Abe Mikell, Webb developed his fundamentals and love of the game.  He was a two-year starter at cornerback and wide receiver.  Webb had seven career interceptions, two of which were returned for scores.  He was named to first-team All-Peninsula District as a cornerback (2007), and earned honorable mention distinction as a junior.

He was also a standout track athlete at Warwick, he ran a career best time of 6.60 seconds in the [[55 metres]]. He excelled in [[triple jump]] and [[long jump]] as well. He was named to the All-America Team in [[track and field]].

==College career==
Webb decided to enroll in the [[College of William & Mary]], where he played for the [[William & Mary Tribe football]] team from 2008 to 2012. After redshirting in 2008, he was honored as the [[Colonial Athletic Association]] (CAA) Defensive Rookie of the Year. He was also selected to the All-CAA second-team as a cornerback and to the all-league third-team as a punt returner. He was tied for second nationally with eight interceptions, including a pair of interceptions returned for touchdowns, and totaled 160 interception return yards.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.tribeathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3556 | title=B.W. Webb bio | access-date=February 19, 2016}}</ref>

In 2010, he was selected to the All-CAA first-team as a cornerback and garnered second-team honors as a punt returner after finished the season with 42 tackles, 0.5 tackles for loss, an interception and six passes broken up. In 2011, he earned first-team all-conference honors at cornerback for the second consecutive season, and finished the season with 40 tackles, 3.0 tackles for a loss and two interceptions.

As a senior, he garnered first-team all-league distinction as a cornerback for the third consecutive season, he also earned second-team all-conference honors as a punt returner.  He finished his career with nine postseason all-conference honors, and set a school record with 48 career starts. He started all 11 games and totaled 46 tackles, two fumble recoveries, a forced fumble, eight passes broken up and a tackle for loss. He was initiated as a member of [[Omega Psi Phi]] fraternity at William and Mary.

===Dallas Cowboys===
The [[Dallas Cowboys]] selected Webb in the fourth round (114th overall) of the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Webb was the 16th cornerback drafted in 2013.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4708089/cowboys-select-cornerback-bw-webb-in-fourth-round | title=Cowboys select cornerback BW Webb in fourth round | date=April 27, 2013 | access-date=February 19, 2016}}</ref>

On May 14, 2013, the Dallas Cowboys signed Webb to a four-year, [[United States dollar|$]]2.60 million [[contract]] that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $443,380.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web |title=Spotrac.com: B.W. Webb contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/new-york-giants/b.w.-webb-12395/ |access-date=November 6, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Cowboys Sign Third Draft Pick, Fourth Round Cornerback B.W. Webb |url=https://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2013/5/14/4332400/dallas-cowboys-sign-fourth-round-cornerback-b-w-webb-salary-cap-rookies-contract-holloman-randle |access-date=November 6, 2018 |website=bloggingtheboys.com |author=Drummond, K.D. |date=May 14, 2013}}</ref>

Webb entered training camp slated as the fourth cornerback on the depth chart.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cowboys position series: Cornerbacks |url=http://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4709990/cowboys-position-series-cornerbacks-3 |access-date=November 6, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |author=MacMahon, Tim |date=July 5, 2013}}</ref> Head coach [[Jason Garrett]] named Webb the fourth cornerback on the depth chart to begin the regular season, behind [[Brandon Carr]], [[Morris Claiborne]], and [[Orlando Scandrick]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Dallas Cowboys Depth Chart: 09/05/2013 |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/150/DAL |access-date=November 6, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the [[2013 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys’]] season-opening 36–31 victory against the [[2013 New York Giants season|New York Giants]]. In Week 8, he collected a season-high three solo tackles and deflected a pass  during a 27–23 win against the [[2013 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]]. Webb saw an increased snap count in Weeks 9–10 after Morris Claiborne was sidelined due to a [[hamstring]] injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Morris Claiborne injury: Cowboys CB suffers setback with hamstring against Giants |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2013/11/24/5141502/morris-claiborne-injury-cowboys-cb-suffers-setback-with-hamstring |access-date=November 6, 2018 |website=sbnation.com |author=Kaye, Mike |date=November 24, 2013}}</ref> On December 9, 2013, Webb had a dismal performance and was benched in favor of [[Sterling Moore]] during a 45–28 loss at the [[2013 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]] in a Week 13. He was surpassed by Sterling Moore on the depth chart and was demoted to the scout team for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=B.W. Webb: Playing "Too Young" |url=https://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2013/12/13/5204748/bw-webb-playing-too-young |access-date=November 6, 2018 |website=bloggingtheboys.com |author=Macelli, Dawn |date=December 13, 2013}}</ref> Webb was inactive as a healthy scratch for the Dallas Cowboys’ 24–22 loss to the [[2013 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] in a Week 17.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: B.W. '''Avery Milton Williamson''' (born March 9, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats football|Kentucky Wildcats]] and was selected by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the fifth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. Williamson was also a member of the [[New York Jets]], [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], and [[Denver Broncos]].

==Early life==
Williamson attended Milan High School in [[Milan, Tennessee]], where he led his team to consecutive 14–1 records as a junior and senior (2008 & 2009), losing only in the state championship finals each year to [[Alcoa High School]]. He recorded 125 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] with one [[interception]] and also [[Rush (gridiron football)|rushed]] for 416 yards and seven [[touchdown]]s. He collected 119 tackles as a junior, including 21 for loss and set a Tennessee state championship game record with 22 tackles in the title contest. He was named the Region Defensive Player of the Year as a junior and senior.

He was rated as a three-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]''.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/kentucky/football/recruiting/player-Avery-Williamson-92457 Avery Williamson – Yahoo Sports]</ref>

==College career==
Williamson attended the [[University of Kentucky]] from [[2010 Kentucky Wildcats football team|2010]] to [[2013 Kentucky Wildcats football team|2013]]. In 2010, he played in all 13 games as a [[true freshman]], totaling 10 tackles and one [[pass break-up]].  In [[2011 Kentucky Wildcats football team|2011]], he played in all 12 games, recording 49 tackles. In [[2012 Kentucky Wildcats football team|2012]], he started all 12 games, finishing second in the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) with 135 tackles, which placed seventh nationally in total tackles. He also recorded 4.5 [[tackles for loss]], three [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], four pass breakups, two forced [[fumbles]], one interception and one fumble recovery. In [[2013 Kentucky Wildcats football team|2013]], in his senior season, he recorded 102 tackles, including four for loss, one sack and two fumble recoveries, and was named a second-team All-SEC selection.<ref>[http://www.nationofblue.com/2013/12/avery-williamson-named-to-all-sec-second-team-defense/ Avery Williamson named to All-SEC second team defense] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140512221955/http://www.nationofblue.com/2013/12/avery-williamson-named-to-all-sec-second-team-defense/ |date=May 12, 2014 }}</ref>

Williamson was selected to play in the 2014 [[NFLPA Collegiate Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/011314aaa.html |title=Avery Williamson to Play in NFLPA Collegiate Bowl |access-date=November 18, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129040640/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/011314aaa.html |archive-date=November 29, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Williamson was one of 35 collegiate linebackers to attend the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]]. He completed all of the essential combine drills and finished third among all [[linebackers]] in the [[short shuttle]], finished sixth in the [[40-yard dash]], tied for eighth in the [[bench press]], ninth in the [[broad jump]], and finished 11th in the [[three-cone drill]].<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Combine 2014: Results - Linebackers| url=https://www.thephinsider.com/2014/2/28/5455896/nfl-combine-2014-results-linebackers| access-date=February 25, 2018| website=thephinsider.com| author=Nogle, Kevin| date=February 28, 2014}}</ref> On March 14, 2014, Williamson attended Kentucky's [[pro day]], but opted to stand on his combine numbers and only performed positional drills for 20 team representatives and scouts from various NFL teams. During the draft process, he attended a private visit with the [[Tennessee Titans]] and [[Washington Redskins]]. At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, Williamson was projected to be a fifth or sixth round pick by [[NFL draft]] experts and scouts.<ref name="draft"/> He was ranked the eighth best inside linebacker prospect in the draft by Matt Miller of [[Bleacher Report]] and NFLDraftScout.com. Miller also named Williamson the biggest sleeper amongst all inside linebackers in the draft.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Draft Big Board 2014: Matt Miller's Final Rankings| url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2040149-nfl-draft-big-board-2014-matt-millers-final-rankings| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=bleacherreport.com}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans (first stint)===
====2014====
The [[Tennessee Titans]] selected Williamson in the fifth round (151st overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Steve |date=May 10, 2014 |title=Titans draft UK's Avery Williamson in Round 5 |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2014/05/10/avery-williamson-taken-by-titans/8940819/ |access-date=2024-01-10 |website=The Courier-Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> He was the 18th linebacker selected in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  May 21, 2014, the Titans signed Williamson to a four-year, $2.41 million contract that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $194,452.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: Avery Williamson contract| url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/tennessee-titans/avery-williamson-14562/| access-date=February 25, 2018| website=spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]], Williamson competed for a roster spot and a role as a backup linebacker against [[Moise Fokou]], [[Zaviar Gooden]], [[Colin McCarthy]], [[Patrick Bailey (American football)|Patrick Bailey]] and [[Brandon Copeland (linebacker)|Brandon Copeland]].<ref>{{cite web| title=5 Tennessee Titans Veterans Who Could Be Camp Casualties| url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2149938-5-tennessee-titans-veterans-who-could-be-camp-casualties| access-date=February 25, 2018| website=bleacherreport.com| author=Minton, Chad| date=August 2, 2014}}</ref> Head coach [[Ken Whisenhunt]] named Williamson the backup inside linebacker behind starters [[Wesley Woodyard]], [[Zach Brown]], and Zaviar Gooden to begin the regular season.<ref>{{cite web| title=2014 Tennessee Titans Virtual Program: Depth-Chart Analysis and X-Factors| url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2187300-2014-tennessee-titans-virtual-program-depth-chart-analysis-and-x-factors| access-date=February 25, 2018| website=bleacherreport.com}}</ref>

Williamson made his professional regular season debut in the season-opening 26–10 victory at the [[Kansas City Chiefs]]. After being relegated to special teams for the first two weeks, Williams was promoted to the reserve inside linebacker on the defense after starter Zach Brown suffered a torn [[pectoralis major muscle|pectoral]] in the season-opener.<ref>{{cite web| title=Titans LB Zach Brown tore pectoral, could miss season| url=https://www.nfl.com/news/titans-lb-zach-brown-tore-pectoral-could-miss-season-0ap3000000391617| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> In Week 3, Williamson recorded his first career tackle and made four combined tackles on 13 defensive snaps as the Titans were routed by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] 33–7. On October 5, 2014, Williamson earned his first career start after surpassing Zaviar Gooden on the depth chart.<ref>{{cite web| title=Titans LB Avery Williamson cutting into time of Zaviar Gooden| url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/titans-lb-avery-williamson-cutting-into-time-of-zaviar-gooden/| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=CBSsports.com| author=Gitlin, Marty| date=October 3, 2014}}</ref> He made seven combined tackles and two pass deflections in a narrow 29–28 loss to the [[Cleveland Browns]] in Week 5. Three weeks later, Williamson made a season-high ten combined tackles, broke up a pass, and recorded his first career sack on quarterback [[Ryan Fitzpatrick]] as the Titans were defeated by the [[Houston Texans]] 30–16.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Game Center: Week 8-2014: Houston Texans @ Tennessee Titans| url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2014102608/2014/REG8/texans@titans| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> On November 17, 2014, Williamson recorded eight combined tackles and sacked [[Ben Roethlisberger]] twice during a 27–24 loss to the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. It marked Williamson's first game with multiple sacks.

Williamson finished his rookie season in 2014 with 79 combined tackles (51 solo), four pass deflections, and three sacks in 16 games and 12 starts.<ref name="career">{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Avery Williamson (career)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/averywilliamson/2543597/careerstats| access-date=February 25, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2015====
After finishing the 2014 season with a 2–14 record, head coach Ken Whisenhunt hired [[Dick LeBeau]] as the assistant head coach and as the co-defensive coordinator with [[Ray Horton]]. Williamson remained as the starting inside linebacker entering camp although Zach Brown returned from injury.<ref>{{cite web| title=Titans' Wesley Woodyard could face diminished role| url=https://www.tennessean.com/31450929| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=tennessean.com| author=Vingan, Adam| date=August 12, 2015}}</ref> He was named the starter, along with Zach Brown and outside linebackers [[Derrick Morgan (American football)|Derrick Morgan]] and [[Brian Orakpo]], to begin the regular season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Tennessee Titans' Depth chart: 10/01/2015| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/176/TEN| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

On October 11, 2015, Williamson recorded nine combined tackles and made his first sack of the season on [[Tyrod Taylor]] during a narrow 14–13 loss to the [[Buffalo Bills]]. Williamson left the game after sustaining a hamstring injury in the fourth quarter and was inactive for the Titans' Week 6 loss to the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Titans LB Avery Williamson questionable vs. Miami Dolphins| url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/story?id=13902987&src=desktop| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=ESPN.com| agency=Associated Press| date=October 13, 2015}}</ref> In Week 7, Williamson recorded five combined tackles, a pass deflection, and made his first career [[interception]] off a pass attempt by [[Matt Ryan (American football)|Matt Ryan]] during the Titans' 10–7 loss to the [[Atlanta Falcons]]. After five consecutive losses head coach Ken Whisenhunt was fired and was replaced with offensive coordinator [[Mike Mularkey]] as interim head coach.<ref>{{cite web| title=Titans fire coach Ken Whisenhunt| url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/14042981/ken-whisenhunt-fired-coach-tennessee-titans| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=ESPN.com| author=Kuharsky, Paul| date=November 4, 2015}}</ref>

On November 15, 2015, Williamson collected a season-high 14 combined tackles (seven solo) and was credited with half a sack on [[Cam Newton]] during a 27–10 loss to the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Avery Williamson (2015)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/averywilliamson/2543597/gamelogs?season=2015| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref> Williamson celebrated his sack on Cam Newton with teammate [[David Bass (American football)|David Bass]] by performing a rendition of the dance from rapper [[Drake (musician)|Drake's]] music video "[[Hotline Bling]]".<ref>{{cite web| title=The same Titan who got mad at Cam Newton for dancing had just danced after sacking Cam Newton| url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2015/11/16/9746034/cam-newton-dance-celebration-titans-panthers-dab| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=sbnation.com| author=Sherman, Rodger| date=November 16, 2015}}</ref> 

Williamson finished his second professional season with 102 combined tackles (63 solo), 3.5 sacks, a pass deflection, and an interception in 15 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.titansonline.com/team/roster/Avery-Williamson/bd09e01c-c914-4b3d-a89a-697300ab0077 |title=Tennessee Titans: Avery Williamson |access-date=April 27, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160526014746/http://www.titansonline.com/team/roster/avery-williamson/bd09e01c-c914-4b3d-a89a-697300ab0077/ |archive-date=May 26, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

====2016====
Head coach Mike Mularkey retained Dick LeBeau and named him the sole coordinator of the defense after [[Ray Horton]] opted to accept the defensive coordinator position with the Browns.<ref>{{cite web| title=Dick LeBeau wanted greater control of Titans defense| url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/nfl/titans/2016/03/21/dick-lebeau-wanted-greater-control-titans-defense/82078456/?from=new-cookie| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=tennessean.com| author=Wolf, Jason| date=March 21, 2016}}</ref> LeBeau retained Williamson and Woodyard as the starting inside linebackers to begin the regular season after [[Zach Brown]] departed for the Bills during [[free agency (sports)|free agency]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Tennessee Titans Depth chart: 10/01/2016| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/188/TEN| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

In Week 3, Williamson recorded nine combined tackles, broke up a pass, and intercepted [[Derek Carr]] during a 17–10 loss to the [[Oakland Raiders]]. The following week, he recorded a season-high 12 combined tackles in the Titans' 27–20 loss at the Texans. On December 11, 2016, Williamson made three combined tackles and forced the first fumble of his career as Tennessee defeated the [[Denver Broncos]] 13–10.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Avery Williamson (2016)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/averywilliamson/2543597/gamelogs?season=2016| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Williamson finished the 2016 season with a career-high 104 combined tackles (73 solo), two sacks, a pass deflection, and an interception in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref name="career" /> The Titans saw significant improvement under their new head coach, going from 3–13 to 9-7 and finishing second in the [[AFC South]], but did not qualify for a playoff berth. Williamson received an overall grade of 76.5 from [[Pro Football Focus]], ranking him 41st among all qualified linebackers in overall grade.<ref>{{cite web| title=Titans could look for ILB upgrade in draft| url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/news/draft-titans-could-look-for-ilb-upgrade-in-draft| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=profootballfocus.com| date=April 27, 2017}}</ref>

====2017====
Woodyard and Williamson returned as the starting inside linebacker duo along with [[Derrick Morgan (American football)|Derrick Morgan]] and [[Brian Orakpo]] to start the regular season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Ourlads.com: Tennessee Titans' depth chart: 10/01/2017| url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/200/TEN| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

On October 22, 2017, Williamson made a career-high tying 14 combined tackles during a 12–9 win at the Browns in Week 7. In Week 15, he made six solo tackles and sacked quarterback [[Jimmy Garoppolo]] in the Titans' narrow 25–23 loss at the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. 

Williamson finished the 2017 season with 92 combined tackles (52 solo), three sacks, and two pass break ups in 16 games and starts.<ref name="career" /> The Titans finished second in the AFC South with a 9–7  record and qualified for a Wildcard spot. On January 6, 2018, Williamson started his first career playoff game and recorded one tackle in the narrow 22–21 victory at the Chiefs in the AFC Wildcard game. The following week, he recorded nine combined tackles and a pass deflection during the Titans' 35–14 loss at the [[New England Patriots]] in the AFC Divisional Round.<ref>{{cite web| title=NFL Player stats: Avery Williamson (2017)| url=http://www.nfl.com/player/averywilliamson/2543597/gamelogs?season=2017| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On January 15, 2018, head coach Mike Mularkey and the Titans agreed to part ways after being unable to come to terms on future plans.<ref>{{cite web| title=Titans part ways with head coach Mike Mularkey| url=http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Part-Ways-with-Head-Coach-Mike-Mularkey/4c8c0172-ab3c-4734-8a02-742f7297c7c8| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=Titansonline.com| date=January 15, 2018| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180225073523/http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Part-Ways-with-Head-Coach-Mike-Mularkey/4c8c0172-ab3c-4734-8a02-742f7297c7c8| archive-date=February 25, 2018| url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Pro Football Focus]] gave Williamson an overall grade of 85.6, which ranked tenth among all qualifying linebackers in 2017.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro Football Focus: Avery Williamson| url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/avery-williamson/8786| access-date=February 26, 2018| website=profootballfocus.com}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
====2018====
On March 18, 2018, the [[New York Jets]] signed Williamson to a three-year, $22.50 million contract that includes $16 million guaranteed and a [[signing bonus]] of $6 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets add linebacker Avery Williamson|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/03/13/jets-add-linebacker-avery-williamson/|author=Gantt, Darin|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=March 13, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/LB-Avery-Williamson-Agrees-to-Deal-with-Jets/d5825e22-4cea-429d-a502-0bb5ec567f2d|title=LB Avery Williamson Agrees to Deal with Jets|work=NYJets.com|first=Eric|last=Allen|date=March 19, 2018|access-date=March 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180320170540/http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-7/LB-Avery-Williamson-Agrees-to-Deal-with-Jets/d5825e22-4cea-429d-a502-0bb5ec567f2d|archive-date=March 20, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/football/nfl/jets-sign-lb-avery-williamson-3-year-22-million-deal/|title=Jets sign linebacker Avery Williamson to 3-year, $22M deal|work=Sportsnet.com|date=March 14, 2018}}</ref><ref name="spotrac"/>

Williamson entered training camp slated as a starting inside linebacker. Head coach [[Todd Bowles]] named Williamson and [[Darron Lee]] the starting inside linebackers to begin the season, alongside outside linebackers [[Josh Martin (American football)|Josh Martin]] and [[Jordan Jenkins]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The 2018 Jets Opening Day Depth Chart |url=https://www.ganggreennation.com/2018/9/4/17810946/the-2018-jets-opening-day-depth-chart |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=ganggreennation.com |date=September 4, 2018}}</ref> On September 20, 2018, Williamson collected a season-high 14 combined tackles (eight solo) and made two sacks during a 21–17 loss at the Browns in Week 3. During Week 6, Williamson made five solo tackles, a season-high three pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Andrew Luck]] in the 42–34 victory over the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Avery Williamson (2018) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/averywilliamson/2543597/gamelogs |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Williamson started in all 16 games in 2018 and recorded a career-high 120 combined tackles (80 solo), six pass deflections, three sacks, and an interception.<ref name="career" />

====2019–2020====
In the second preseason game against the [[Atlanta Falcons]] on August 15, Williamson left the game with an apparent knee injury. The next day, it was revealed that he tore his ACL, prematurely ending his 2019 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Avery Williamson tore his ACL|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/08/16/avery-williamson-tore-his-acl/|author=Alper, Josh|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=August 16, 2019}}</ref> He was placed on the active/[[physically unable to perform list]] at the start of training camp on July 30, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Lange, Randy |title=Four Jets Veterans Placed on to Active Injury Lists |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/four-jets-veterans-placed-on-to-active-injury-lists |website=NewYorkJets.com |date=July 30, 2020 |access-date=July 30, 2020}}</ref> He was activated on August 22, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Aber, Spencer |title=Jets activate Avery Williamson, Ryan Griffin, Daniel Brown |url=https://jetswire.usatoday.com/2020/08/22/jets-activate-avery-williamson-ryan-griffin-daniel-brown/ |website=USAToday.com |date=August 22, 2020 |access-date=August 23, 2020}}</ref>

In Week 8 of the 2020 season against the Chiefs, Williamson's last game as a Jet, he recorded a team high 9 tackles during the 35–9 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Jets at Kansas City Chiefs - November 1st, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011010kan.htm |access-date=2020-11-04 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On November 1, 2020, Williamson was traded to the Steelers along with the Jets' 2022 seventh-round pick for the Steelers' 2022 fifth-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Jets trade LB Avery Williamson to Pittsburgh Steelers|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/30241509/new-york-jets-trade-lb-avery-williamson-pittsburgh-steelers|author=Cimini, Rich|work=ESPN|date=November 1, 2020}}</ref> In Week 16 against the Colts, he recorded a team high 14 tackles and sacked [[Philip Rivers]] once during the 28–24 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Pittsburgh Steelers - December 27th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012270pit.htm |access-date=2020-12-30 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos (first stint)===
On October 5, 2021, Williamson was signed to the Broncos [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos sign ILB Avery Williamson and WR Josh Malone to practice squad|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-ilb-avery-williamson-and-wr-josh-malone-to-practice-squad|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=October 5, 2021|access-date=October 7, 2021|archive-date=October 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211023135821/https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-ilb-avery-williamson-and-wr-josh-malone-to-practice-squad|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans (second stint)===
On October 13, 2021, Williamson was signed by the Titans off the Broncos practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Sign LB Avery Williamson, Move S Amani Hooker to "Designated for Return from Injured Reserve" List|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-lb-avery-williamson-move-s-amani-hooker-to-designated-for-return-fro|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=October 13, 2021}}</ref> On November 2, Williamson was released from the active roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Sign Veteran RBs Adrian Peterson and D'Onta Foreman to Practice Squad in a Flurry of Moves|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-veteran-rbs-adrian-peterson-and-d-onta-foreman-to-practice-squad-in-|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=November 2, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos (second stint)===
On November 9, 2021, Williamson was re-signed to the Broncos practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |author=DiLalla, Aric |date=November 9, 2021 |title=Broncos promote G Austin Schlottmann to active roster, place G Graham Glasgow on IR |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-promote-g-austin-schlottmann-to-active-roster-place-g-graham-glasgow-on- |access-date=April 19, 2026 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> He was released on December 23.

'''Austin Wentworth''' (born May 10, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive guard]] for one season with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Fresno State Bulldogs football]] and attended [[Whitney High School (Rocklin, California)|Whitney High School]] in [[Rocklin, California]].

==Early life==
Wentworth played [[high school football]] for the Whitney High School Wildcats. He earned Pioneer Valley League lineman of the year as the Wildcats finished with an 11–2 record, was named First-team All-PVC twice, first-team All-metro, first-team All-state, Whitney High School Athlete of the Year and played in the KCRA3 All-Star Classic. He also [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] in [[track & field]] as a thrower in the [[shot put]] (47-11 or 14.62m) and the [[discus]] (131-5 or 40.13m).<ref name="A">{{cite web|url=http://www.gobulldogs.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/austin_wentworth_460870.html |title=72Austin Wentworth |publisher=gobulldogs.com |access-date=October 27, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141027201019/http://www.gobulldogs.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/austin_wentworth_460870.html |archive-date=October 27, 2014 }}</ref>

==College career==
Wentworth played for the [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Bulldogs]] at [[California State University, Fresno]], from 2010 to 2013. He was [[redshirted]] in 2009.<ref name="A"/> He was named ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' honorable mention [[All-American]] following his senior season. He was a two-time 1st-Team All-[[Mountain West]] selection and finished his career with 43 starts, including 42 consecutive.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.vikings.com/team/roster/austin-wentworth/19fb3f17-332d-4319-977f-8b97fe581c73/ | title=Austin Wentworth | publisher=vikings.com | access-date=October 27, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141122174901/http://www.vikings.com/team/roster/Austin-Wentworth/19fb3f17-332d-4319-977f-8b97fe581c73 | archive-date=November 22, 2014 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==
Wentworth signed with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] on May 11, 2014, after going undrafted in the [[2014 NFL draft]]. He was released by the Vikings on August 31 and re-signed to the team on September 2, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kffl.com/player/29897/nfl/news |title=Austin Wentworth |publisher=kffl.com |access-date=October 27, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141204184608/http://www.kffl.com/player/29897/nfl/news |archive-date=December 4, 2014 }}</ref> He made his NFL debut on October 26, 2014, against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WentAu01/gamelog// | title=Austin Wentworth | publisher=Sports Reference LLC | work=pro-football-reference.com | access-date=October 27, 2014}}</ref> Wentworth was released by the Vikings on May 7, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/north/story/minnesota-vikings-release-five-players-to-make-room-on-offseason-roster-050715 |title=Vikings release five players to make room on offseason roster |work=foxsports.com |date=May 7, 2015 |access-date=May 8, 2015 |author=Hall, Brian |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150508133836/http://www.foxsports.com/north/story/minnesota-vikings-release-five-players-to-make-room-on-offseason-roster-050715 |archive-date=May 8, 2015 }}</ref>

On May 13, 2015, it was reported that he was retiring due to [[blood clots]] in his leg. After surgery, he lost the muscle in his left leg that controlled the up function of his foot and will have to wear a brace for the rest of his life.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.twincities.com/sports/ci_28107031/vikings-austin-wentworths-nfl-career-ends |title=Vikings: Austin Wentworth says clots in leg ended his NFL career |publisher=twincities.com |date=May 13, 2015 |access-date=May 13, 2015 |author=Tomasson, Chris |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150514014116/http://www.twincities.com/sports/ci_28107031/vikings-austin-wentworths-nfl-career-ends |archive-date=May 14, 2015 }}</ref>

'''B. J. Dubose''' (born January 19, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]]. He played [[college football]] at [[University of Louisville]]. He was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the sixth round of the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Christopher |last=Gates |title=2015 NFL Draft Results: Minnesota Vikings Select B.J. Dubose |url=http://www.dailynorseman.com/2015/5/2/8534941/2015-nfl-draft-results-minnesota-vikings-select-b-j-dubose |work=Daily Norseman |publisher=Vox Media |date=May 2, 2015 |accessdate=May 4, 2015 }}</ref>

==Early life==
Born in [[Oakland Park, Florida]], Dubose attended [[Northeast High School (Oakland Park, Florida)|Northeast High School]] in his hometown. He notched 55 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]], 11 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] and three forced fumbles as a junior en route to third-team All-State accolades. As a senior, he recorded 60 tacklesto go along with 11 [[quarterback sack|sacks]]. Dubose also participated in [[track & field]] at Northeast, competing in the throwing events and posting top-throws of 11.85 meters (38 feet, 9 inches) in the [[shot put]] and 32.12 meters (105 feet, 4 inches) in the [[discus]] at the 2011 BCAA North Central Qualifier.<ref>{{cite web | title=BCAA North Central Qualifier 2011 | website=flrunners.com | date=2011-03-22 | url=https://fl.milesplit.com/meets/83669-bcaa-north-central-qualifier-2011/results/151368 | access-date=2025-10-24}}</ref>

Regarded as a three-star prospect by [[Rivals.com]], Dubose was ranked as the No. 24 [[defensive end]] in the Rivals poll of best and was 64th in the Florida postseason top 100.

==College career==
Dubose narrowed his college choice to [[Louisville Cardinals football|Louisville]], [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan]] and [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami]], choosing the Cardinals and [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] in 2010. He saw three starts in 2011 as a [[redshirt freshman]], recording 22 tackles, 3.5 [[tackles for loss]] and 2.0 sacks. Dubose started four games in 2012 as a [[sophomore]] and finished with 15 tackles and 0.5 tackle for loss. He didn't start a game as a [[Junior (education year)|junior]], but played in 11 contests and recorded 16 tackles, 4.0 tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks. Dubose returned to the starting line-up as a [[Senior (education)|senior]] in 2014, finishing with 41 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss, and 4.0 sacks. He earned an invitation to the [[2015 East-West Shrine Game]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/2028311/bj-dubose |title=Archived copy |access-date=May 11, 2015 |archive-date=May 18, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518092022/http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/2028311/bj-dubose |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Ayanga Okpokowuruk''' (born June 19, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player. He played [[college football]] at [[Duke University]] and attended [[The McCallie School]] in [[Chattanooga, Tennessee]]. He was a member of the [[New York Giants]], [[Spokane Shock]], [[Cleveland Browns]], [[Arizona Rattlers]] and [[Jacksonville Sharks]].

==Early life==
Okpokowuruk was a four-year [[Letterman (sports)|letterman]] for The McCallie School Blue Tornadoes. He earned all-state and all-city honors his senior year in 2004 after recording 39 tackles and five sacks as the team went 8-3 and advanced to the state semifinals. He recorded 30 tackles and four sacks while catching 12 passes for 210 yards and one touchdown his junior season, being named honorable mention all-state as the Blue Tornadoes finished with a 7-5 record and state semifinal berth. Okpokowuruk also participated in basketball and [[track and field]], placing fourth in the state in the [[shot put]] competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=157430 |title=AYANGA OKPOKOWURUK |publisher=goduke.com |accessdate=May 4, 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505000453/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=157430 |archivedate=May 5, 2015 }}</ref>

==College career==
Okpokowuruk played for the [[Duke Blue Devils football|Duke Blue Devils]] from 2005 to 2009. He played in 47 games, recording 108 tackles, 10.5 sacks and two forced fumbles.<ref name="A">{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafootball.com/sports/a-footbl/aflsrk/mtt/ayanga_okpokowuruk_831092.html |title=Ayanga Okpokowuruk |publisher=arenafootball.com |accessdate=May 4, 2015 |url-status=usurped |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505002614/http://www.arenafootball.com/sports/a-footbl/aflsrk/mtt/ayanga_okpokowuruk_831092.html |archivedate=May 5, 2015 }}</ref>

==Professional career==
Okpokowuruk signed with the [[New York Giants]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) on April 24, 2010 after going undrafted in the [[2010 NFL draft]].<ref name="y640">{{cite web | title=Former McCallie Lineman Okpokowuruk Inks With NY Giants | website=Chattanoogan.com | date=2010-04-27 | url=https://www.chattanoogan.com/2010/4/26/174350/Former-McCallie-Lineman-Okpokowuruk.aspx | access-date=2024-11-10}}</ref> He was released by the Giants on July 30, 2010. He signed a future contracts with the Giants on January 13, 2011, and was released by the team on September 3, 2011.<ref name="B">{{cite web|url=http://www.kffl.com/player/23084/nfl/news/ayanga-okpokowuruk |title=Ayanga Okpokowuruk |publisher=kffl.com |accessdate=May 4, 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505003121/http://www.kffl.com/player/23084/nfl/news/ayanga-okpokowuruk |archivedate=May 5, 2015 }}</ref>

Okpokowuruk was assigned to the [[Spokane Shock]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) on May 26, 2011.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=149 | title=Historical Team Transactions | publisher=arenafan.com | accessdate=May 4, 2015}}</ref> He appeared in six games for the Shock during the [[2011 Arena Football League season|2011 season]], recording eight tackles and a sack.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafootball.com/sports/a-footbl/spec-rel/113012aaa.html |title=Rattlers Assigned DL Okpokowuruk |publisher=arenafootball.com |accessdate=May 4, 2015 |url-status=usurped |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505004513/http://www.arenafootball.com/sports/a-footbl/spec-rel/113012aaa.html |archivedate=May 5, 2015 }}</ref>

On November 29, 2011, the [[Cleveland Browns]] of the NFL signed Okpokowuruk  to the team's practice squad.<ref name="B"/>

Okpokowuruk was assigned to the AFL's [[Arizona Rattlers]] on November 29, 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=21 |title=Historical Team Transactions |publisher=arenafan.com |accessdate=May 4, 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150314200853/http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=21 |archivedate=March 14, 2015 }}</ref>

Okpokowuruk was traded to the [[Jacksonville Sharks]] on March 16, 2013.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=139 | title=Historical Team Transactions | publisher=arenafan.com | accessdate=May 4, 2015}}</ref> He recorded 3.5 tackles for the Sharks in 2013.<ref name="A"/>

'''Benjamin J. Isaac Finney II''' (born October 26, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State Wildcats]], and was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in 2015.

Finney also played for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] and the [[Seattle Seahawks]].

==Early life==
Finney was born in [[Wichita, Kansas]]. He attended high school at Andale High School in the Wichita suburb of [[Andale, Kansas|Andale]]. He was an unranked two-star recruit for the class of 2010. He committed to [[Kansas State University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=BJ Finney recruiting profile |url=https://247sports.com/Player/BJ-Finney-34602/high-school-56307/ |website=247sports.com}}</ref> He was a state [[wrestling]] champ his senior year.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mueller |first=Chris B. |date=September 1, 2016 |title=B.J. Finney, a former state champion wrestler, hoping strides will lead him to 53-man roster |language=en |work=The Times |url=https://www.timesonline.com/63c7b742-6fb0-11e6-8975-9f27a498b127.html |access-date=October 29, 2020 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==College career==
Finney [[redshirted]] his freshman year at [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State]]. His redshirt freshman year he started in 12 games, only missing the first game. He was named [[List of All-Big 12 Conference football teams|All-Big 12 Conference]] twice, honorable mention as a sophomore<ref>{{cite web |title=2012 Football All-Big 12 Awards Announcement |url=https://big12sports.com/news/2012/12/5/205820514.aspx |website=Big12Sports.com|date=December 5, 2012 }}</ref> and first-team as a senior.<ref>{{cite web |title=All-Big 12 Football Awards Announced |url=https://big12sports.com/news/2014/12/10/209801479.aspx |website=Big12Sports.com|date=December 10, 2014 }}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Coming out of Kansas State, Finney was projected to be selected in the fourth or fifth round by the majority of [[NFL draft]] experts and scouts.<ref name="draft">{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/draft/2015/profiles/b.j.-finney?id=2552238| title=NFL Draft Profile: B.J. Finney| access-date=October 16, 2017| website=NFL.com}}</ref> He received an invitation to the [[NFL Combine]] and completed nearly all the required combine drills, only missing the [[three-cone drill]] due to a back injury. On March 10, 2015, he participated at Kansas State's [[pro day]] and opted to stand on his combine numbers and only perform positional drills for the team representatives and scouts from 15 NFL teams. Along with Finney, [[Tyler Lockett]], Curry Sexton, and seven other draft prospects attended Kansas State's pro day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bengals-coach-watches-tyler-lockett-at-kansas-state-pro-day-0ap3000000479113| title=Bengals coach watches Tyler Lockett at Kansas State pro day| access-date=October 16, 2017| website=NFL.com| author=Gil Brandt| date=March 15, 2015}}</ref> He was ranked as the third best [[Center (football)|center]] available on the draft by NFLDraftScout.com. NFL Draft analysts and scouts referred to him as a "plug and play" starter.<ref name="draft"/>

===Pittsburgh Steelers (first stint)===
====2015====
The [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] signed Finney as an undrafted rookie free agent immediately following the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers agree to terms with 12 rookie free agents|url=http://www.steelers.com/news/article-1/Steelers-agree-to-terms-with-12-rookie-free-agents/e0a53180-101d-4122-b1de-08fe9c0f4150|website=Steelers.com|date=May 2, 2015|access-date=July 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170904013749/http://www.steelers.com/news/article-1/Steelers-agree-to-terms-with-12-rookie-free-agents/e0a53180-101d-4122-b1de-08fe9c0f4150|archive-date=September 4, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> Even though he was a highly sought after undrafted free agent, he opted to sign with the Steelers as they were his favorite NFL team as a child. Finney's surprising fall in the draft was said to be in part due to teams' fearing his arms were too short and that he lacked technique and athleticism.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.pittsburgh.cbslocal.com/2015/05/05/video-undrafted-free-agent-makes-emotional-announcement-signs-with-steelers/| title=VIDEO: Undrafted Free Agent Makes Emotional Announcement, Signs With Steelers| access-date=October 16, 2017| website=Pittsburgh.Cbslocal.com| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160331125706/http://pittsburgh.cbslocal.com/2015/05/05/video-undrafted-free-agent-makes-emotional-announcement-signs-with-steelers/| archive-date=March 31, 2016| url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stillcurtain.com/2016/10/06/steelers-player-spotlight-bj-finney/| title=Steelers Player Spotlight: BJ Finney| access-date=October 16, 2017| website=stillcurtain.com| author=Jack Tolman| date=October 3, 2015}}</ref>

Finney competed with fellow rookie [[Reese Dismukes]] and veteran [[Cody Wallace]] to be the Steelers' backup center behind [[Maurkice Pouncey]]. On September 3, 2015, he left the Steelers final preseason game against the [[Carolina Panthers]] with an injury.

As a result, Finney was waived with an injury designation and subsequently reverted to the Steelers' [[injured reserve]] list before being released with an injury settlement on September 5, 2015. On September 29, 2015, the Steelers signed Finney to their [[practice squad]] after releasing [[Barrett Jones]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers reduce roster to 53 players; sign cornerback Ross Cockrell|url=http://www.steelers.com/news/transactions/article-1/Steelers-reduce-roster-to-53-players-sign-cornerback-Ross-Cockrell/805b9ee2-caaa-4f20-b161-4e36d0811b3a|website=Steelers.com|date=September 5, 2015|access-date=March 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170903120827/http://www.steelers.com/news/transactions/article-1/Steelers-reduce-roster-to-53-players-sign-cornerback-Ross-Cockrell/805b9ee2-caaa-4f20-b161-4e36d0811b3a|archive-date=September 3, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://steelcityblitz.com/b-j-finney-a-pittsburgh-steeler-once-again-this-time-on-the-practice-squad/| title=B.J. Finney A Pittsburgh Steeler Once Again. This Time On The Practice Squad| access-date=October 16, 2017| website=steelcityblitz.com| author=Ben Anderson| date=September 29, 2015}}</ref>

====2016====
Finney entered his training camp in 2016 competing with Wallace, Cole Manhart, and [[Chris Hubbard]] for the job to be backup [[offensive guard]] or center. He was named the third string offensive guard behind [[Ramon Foster]] and Hubbard to begin his second season and the third string center behind Pouncey and Wallace.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/188/PIT| title=Ourlads.com: Pittsburgh Steelers depth chart: 10/01/2016| access-date=October 16, 2017| website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>  On January 18, 2016, the Steelers signed him to a reserve/future contract.

On October 2, 2016, Finney received his first career start against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] after left guard Foster was unable to play due to injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/blog/pittsburgh-steelers/post/_/id/20484/dream-come-true-b-j-finney-jordan-dangerfield-improbable-starters-for-pittsburgh-steelers|title=Finney, Dangerfield, improbable starters for Pittsburgh Steelers|date=October 2, 2016 |access-date=October 2, 2016}}</ref> He finished the season with three starts in 13 games.

====2017====
He competed with [[Ethan Cooper]] and Lucas Crowley for the backup offensive guard position and competed with Mike Matthews and [[Kyle Friend]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/198/PIT| title=Ourlads.com: Pittsburgh Steelers depth chart: 08/01/2017| access-date=October 16, 2017| website=ourlads.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Mike Tomlin]] named Finney the backup center to Pouncey and the backup left guard to Foster to begin the regular season.

On October 15, 2017, Finney earned his first start of the 2017 season, helping the Steelers defeat the Chiefs 19–13. He started at left guard in place of Foster, who was out with a back injury.<ref>{{cite web | last=Bryan | first=Dave | title=Steelers C/G B.J. Finney Carted Off Practice Field Thursday | website=Steelers Depot | date=2017-08-17 | url=https://steelersdepot.com/2017/08/steelers-cg-b-j-finney-carted-off-practice-field-thursday-injury/ | access-date=2025-10-05}}</ref>

====2018====
Finney entered the 2018 season as a backup guard. He played in all 16 games, starting two at right guard in place of an injured [[David DeCastro]].

====2019====
On March 6, 2019, the Steelers placed a second-round restricted free agent tender on Finney.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers place second-round tender on B.J. Finney|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/03/06/steelers-place-second-round-tender-on-b-j-finney/|author=Williams, Charean|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=March 6, 2019}}</ref> He played in all 16 games, making 4 starts.

===Seattle Seahawks===
On March 23, 2020, Finney signed a two-year, $8 million contract with the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-offensive-lineman-b-j-finney|work=Seahawks.com|date=March 23, 2020|access-date=March 23, 2020|title=Seahawks Sign Offensive Lineman B.J. Finney|first=John|last=Boyle}}</ref> He played in 6 games for the Seahawks before being traded.

===Cincinnati Bengals===
On October 28, 2020, Finney and a seventh-round draft pick in the [[2021 NFL draft]] were traded to the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] for defensive end [[Carlos Dunlap]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cincinnati Bengals trade DE Carlos Dunlap to Seattle Seahawks|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/cincinnati-bengals-trade-de-carlos-dunlap-to-seattle-seahawks|author=Patra, Kevin|website=NFL.com|date=October 28, 2020}}</ref> Finney was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the Bengals on November 25, 2020,<ref>{{cite news |title=Tate, Finney & Rose Among Midweek Moves |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/tate-finney-rose-among-midweek-moves |website=Bengals.com |date=November 25, 2020 |access-date=December 31, 2020}}</ref> and activated on November 28.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bengals Player Moves Ahead Of Week 12 |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-player-moves-ahead-of-week-12 |website=Bengals.com |date=November 28, 2020 |access-date=December 31, 2020}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/[[non-football injury list]] on December 31, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=B.J. Finney|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/03/05/bengals-release-b-j-finney/|access-date=March 5, 2021|website=ProFootballTalk|language=en-US}}</ref> Finney's only appearance with the Bengals was on November 15, 2020 against the Steelers.

===Pittsburgh Steelers (second stint)===
Finney signed a one-year contract with the Steelers on March 12, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |author=Varley, Teresa |title=Finney signed to a one-year contract |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/finney-signed-to-a-one-year-contract |website=Steelers.com |date=March 12, 2021 |access-date=March 12, 2021}}</ref> He suffered a back injury in Week 13 and was placed on injured reserve on December 15.

He retired on June 7, 2022.

'''Austin Wheatley''' (born November 16, 1977) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]]. He was selected in the fifth round of the [[2000 NFL draft]] by the [[New Orleans Saints]].

==Early life==
Wheatley was born in [[Milan, Illinois]] and attended [[Rock Island High School]] in [[Rock Island, Illinois]]. While there, he [[Varsity letter|lettered]] in football as well as track and field. He was named First-team Division 5A All-State, All-Metro and All-Conference as both a tight end and [[Punter (football)|punter]]. He was named to the Top 100 Illinois Seniors by the ''Champaign News-Gazette'' as a tight end. In 1994, he averaged 43 yards-per-punt and recorded nine [[Reception (gridiron football)|reception]]s for 271 yards with three [[touchdown]]s. He also set a school record with a 68-yard punt.

While at Rock Island, Wheatley was also a member of the [[National Honor Society]].

==College career==
Wheatley attended [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa]] where he played both tight end and punter. As a freshman in 1995, he [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] and was named the offensive scout team MVP against [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin]].  In 1996, he played sparingly as a tight end and on special teams but recorded no statistics. In 1997, he played as a tight end and punter, early in the season. Midway through the season, he suffered and [[hand]] injury. For the season, as a tight end, he recorded seven receptions for 108 yards and one touchdown and as a punter he punted the ball five times with an average of 41 yards and the longest being 59 yards.<ref name="College stats">{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/austin-wheatley-1.html |title=Austin Wheatley Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=April 24, 2016}}</ref> Two of his five punts where downed inside the 20-yard line. He was named Special teams MVP against [[Northern Iowa Panthers football|Northern Iowa]] and awarded the Offensive Hustle Award against [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois]]. In 1998, he appeared in 11 games with one start, against [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana]]. For the season he recorded nine receptions for 137 yards.<ref name="College stats" /> He was awarded the Offensive Hustle award against [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State]]. As a senior in 1999, he appeared in 11 games with three starts. He recorded nine receptions for 103 yards.<ref name="College stats" />

While at Iowa, Wheatley majored in art.

==Professional career==
Wheatley was selected in the fifth round (158th overall) [[2000 NFL draft]] by the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2000 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2000/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-19 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> As a rookie, he appeared in the first four games of the 2000 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Wheatley 2000 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WheaAu20/gamelog/2000/ |access-date=2025-05-11 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On August 28, 2001, he was released by the Saints.<ref name="Transactions">{{cite web |url=http://www.kffl.com/player/548/nfl |title=Austin Weatley, TE, Free agent |work=KFFL.com |access-date=April 24, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160425090110/http://www.kffl.com/player/548/nfl |archive-date=April 25, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On October 5, 2001, he was signed by the [[Denver Broncos]] to their [[practice squad]].<ref name="Transactions" /> He was released 11 days later on October 16.<ref name="Transactions" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2001/10/17/sports/transactions-715980.html |title=Transactions - NYTimes |work=[[The New York Times]]|date=October 17, 2001 |access-date=April 24, 2016}}</ref> On December 26, 2001, he was signed by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] to their practice squad.<ref name="Transactions" /> On May 23, 2002, he was released by the Cowboys.<ref name="Transactions" /> On October 2, 2002, he was signed by the [[Oakland Raiders]] to their practice squad.<ref name="Transactions" /> He was released a week later.<ref name="Transactions" />

==Personal life==
On January 29, 2001, Wheatley and teammate [[Tutan Reyes]] where summoned to appear in court in regards to the beating of two men.<ref name="Court">{{cite web |url=http://www.kffl.com/player/548/nfl/news |title=Austin Wheatley news, rumors and stats |work=KFFL.com |access-date=April 24, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160425092952/http://www.kffl.com/player/548/nfl/news |archive-date=April 25, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The two players were alleged to have chased the two men after someone had broken into Reye's [[Chevrolet Suburban]] at Wheatley's apartment complex.<ref name="Court" /> The victims alleged they were assaulted without warning.<ref name="Court" /> Deputies said the two were not involved in the break-in.<ref name="Court" />

'''B.J. Goodson''' (born May 29, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] and was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the fourth round of the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Giants draft middle linebacker of the future |first=Paul |last=Schwartz |date=April 30, 2016 |work=[[New York Post]] |url=https://nypost.com/2016/04/30/giants-draft-middle-linebacker-of-the-future/ }}</ref>

==Early life==
A native of [[Lamar, South Carolina]], Goodson attended [[Lamar High School (South Carolina)|Lamar High School]] where he played [[linebacker]], [[tight end]], and [[kick returner]].<ref name="Robinson2015">{{cite news |title=B.J. Goodson was molded in tiny Lamar football factory |first=Manie |last=Robinson |date=December 26, 2015 |work=[[Greenville News]] |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/college/clemson/2015/12/26/clemson-football-swinney-goodson-linebacker-lamar-sc-levon-kirkland/77915936/ }}</ref> An All-State selection in his junior year, Goodson was credited with 96 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] and six [[tackles for loss]] and added 16 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 220 yards and two [[touchdown]]s on offense. Lamar finished the 2009 season with a 12–2 record as the [[South Carolina High School League|SCHSL]] Class A runner-up, losing 36–6 to [[Steve Taneyhill]]'s [[Chesterfield High School (South Carolina)|Chesterfield]] in the state championship game.<ref>{{cite news |title=S.C. football playoff results; updated schedule |work=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]] |date=November 28, 2009 |url=http://www.thestate.com/sports/high-school/article14360606.html }}</ref> In his senior year, Goodson recorded 156 tackles on the season and was invited to the North-South All-Star Game in [[Myrtle Beach, South Carolina]].

Regarded as a three-star recruit by [[ESPN]], Goodson was ranked as the No. 29 [[outside linebacker]] prospect in the class of 2011.<ref>{{cite web |title=2011 ESPN Top Outside linebackers |publisher=ESPN |url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/playerrankings/_/position/outside-linebacker/class/2011/view/position }}</ref> He verbally committed to [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]] on the eve of his senior season, over [[Athletic scholarship|scholarship]] offers from [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee]] and [[LSU Tigers football|Louisiana State]], among others.<ref name="Robinson2015" />

==College career==
After [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his initial year at [[Clemson University]], Goodson steadily progressed from a backup linebacker and valuable [[special teams]] player to starting linebacker and leading tackler of the Tigers defense. Appearing in 47 career games with 21 starts, he was credited with 205 tackles, 17.5 tackles for loss, 6.5 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], 21 quarterback pressures, five [[pass breakups]] and five recovered [[fumble]]s.

Goodson, Olivier Vernon |url=https://giantswire.usatoday.com/2017/09/26/new-york-giants-injury-report-b-j-goodson-olivier-vernon-orleans-darkwa/ |access-date=January 15, 2019 |website=USA Today |date=September 26, 2017}}</ref> In Week 6, he recorded six combined tackles and made a season-high two pass deflections in the Giants' 23–10 victory at the [[Denver Broncos]].
