'''Avery Moss''' (born September 16, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska Cornhuskers]] and [[Youngstown State Penguins football|Youngstown State Penguins]], and was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the fifth round of the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>[http://www.omaha.com/huskers/blogs/nfl-draft-new-york-giants-take-former-husker-avery-moss/article_1aa71a56-2d08-11e7-8ae0-4b4bfdc770e6.html NFL draft: New York Giants take former Husker Avery Moss in fifth round | Big Red Today blog | omaha.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref><ref>[http://newyork.cbslocal.com/2017/04/29/giants-final-draft-day/ N.Y. Giants Select Defensive End Avery Moss In Third Day Of Draft « CBS New York<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

== Early life ==
Moss played [[high school football]] at [[Corona del Sol High School]]. Moss was a three-star recruit coming out of high school and committed to [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln|Nebraska]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Avery Moss, Corona Del Sol , Weak-Side Defensive End|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Avery-Moss-12245/high-school-4877/|access-date=2020-08-30|website=247Sports|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Nebraska 2012 Football Commits|url=https://247sports.com/college/nebraska/Season/2012-Football/Commits/|access-date=2020-08-30|website=247Sports|language=en-US}}</ref>

== College career ==
Moss played football at [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska]] from 2012–2013 and [[Youngstown State Penguins football|Youngstown State]] from 2015–2016.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Avery Moss Bio|url=http://www.nmnathletics.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205371471&DB_OEM_ID=100|access-date=2020-08-30|website=Huskers.com|language=en}}{{Dead link|date=November 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Avery Moss|url=https://www.ysusports.com/sports/fball/2016-17/bios/moss_avery_lntp|access-date=2020-08-30|website=Youngstown State|language=en}}</ref> Moss did not play in 2014 after being banned from Nebraska's campus for indecent exposure.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ristau|first=Reece|title=Nebraska football player Avery Moss banned from campus through 2014|url=http://www.dailynebraskan.com/sports/nebraska-football-player-avery-moss-banned-from-campus-through-2014/article_a48c7e46-87d4-11e3-981f-001a4bcf6878.html|access-date=2020-08-30|website=The Daily Nebraskan|date=January 28, 2014 |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
=== New York Giants ===
Moss was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the fifth round, 167th overall, in the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Giants Draft Youngstown State DE Avery Moss in Round 5|url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-Draft-Youngstown-State-DE-Avery-Moss-in-Round-5/fb88cedc-f902-4cfa-bc0a-b0d532327dd3|author=Salomone, Dan|website=Giants.com|date=April 29, 2017|accessdate=May 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502100911/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-Draft-Youngstown-State-DE-Avery-Moss-in-Round-5/fb88cedc-f902-4cfa-bc0a-b0d532327dd3|archive-date=May 2, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Moss forced his first career [[fumble]] against the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on October 22, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Seattle Seahawks at New York Giants - October 22nd, 2017|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710220nyg.htm|access-date=2020-08-30|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref>

On September 1, 2018, Moss was waived by the Giants and was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Giants announce 53-man roster|url=https://www.giants.com/news/new-york-giants-announce-53-man-roster|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=September 1, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Giants waive QB Davis Webb, announce practice squad among roster moves|url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-waive-qb-davis-webb-announce-practice-squad-among-roster-moves|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=September 2, 2018}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Giants on January 14, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants sign DE Avery Moss, G Chad Slade to reserve/future contracts|url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-sign-de-avery-moss-g-chad-slade-to-reserve-future-contracts|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=January 14, 2019}}</ref>

Moss was released by the Giants on September 1, 2019, during final roster cuts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/nfl/new-york-giants/Article/New-York-Giants-roster-cuts-Avery-Moss-121268972/|title=Report: Giants waive 2017 fifth-round draft pick Avery Moss|website=New York Giants|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-02}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On September 1, 2019, Moss was claimed off waivers by the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins Claim Five Players Off Waivers|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-claim-five-players-off-waivers-2019|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=September 1, 2019}}</ref> The Dolphins waived him on July 26, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-waive-trent-harris-avery-moss|work=MiamiDolphins.com|title=Miami Dolphins Waive Trent Harris, Avery Moss|date=July 26, 2020|accessdate=July 26, 2020}}</ref>

Moss was re-signed on August 27, 2020,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dolphins Activate Xavien Howard, Sign Avery Moss|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-activate-xavien-howard-sign-avery-moss|access-date=August 27, 2020|website=MiamiDolphins.com|language=en-US}}</ref> but was waived five days later.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Williams|first=Charean|date=September 1, 2020|title=Dolphins cut four players, including Deatrick Nichols and Avery Moss|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/09/01/dolphins-cut-four-players-including-deatrick-nichols-and-avery-moss/|access-date=September 1, 2020|website=ProFootballTalk|language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Aviante Collins''' (born April 21, 1993) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]]. He played [[college football]] at [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU]].

==Early life==
Collins attended [[Willowridge High School (Houston)|Willowridge High School]] in [[Houston, Texas]], where he was a three-year letterman in [[american football|football]] and a four-year letterwinner in [[track and field]]. He finished third in the shot put at the Class 5A state championships as a sophomore and junior and took fourth as a senior (56'1"). He was the regional champion in the [[shot put]] as a senior with a personal-best mark of 59'1/2".<ref>{{cite web|title=TRACK Deer Park shot putter has shot at state title after strong regional effort|url=https://www.chron.com/neighborhood/deerpark/sports/article/TRACK-Deer-Park-shot-putter-has-shot-at-state-9387000.php|website=Chron.com|date=May 1, 2012}}</ref>

Collins was viewed as a three-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'' at offensive tackle, and was ranked as the No. 175 recruit in the state of [[Texas]] and the No. 91 offensive tackle overall in the nation. After initially committing to [[Houston Cougars football|Houston]], he ultimately decided to play college football at [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU]], turning down scholarship offers from the Cougars and [[Arizona State Sun Devils|Arizona State]].

==College career==
Collins accepted a football scholarship from [[Texas Christian University]]. As true freshman in 2012, he started all 13 games. He began the season at [[left tackle]], before being moved to [[right tackle]].<ref name="n910">{{cite web | last=Ubben | first=David | title=Frogs' 2012 freshman class was 'different' | website=ESPN.com | date=2013-04-10 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/big12/post/_/id/65806/frogs-2012-freshman-class-was-different | access-date=2024-10-11}}</ref>

As a sophomore in 2013, he started 9 contests, the first three at left tackle and the final six at right tackle. As a junior in 2014, he was passed on the depth chart by [[Tayo Fabuluje]] at left tackle and Collins was moved to right tackle behind [[Joseph Noteboom]]. He appeared in  8 games with one start.<ref>{{cite web|title=Spring depth chart analysis: TCU|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/colleges/post/_/id/4688764/depth-chart-analysis-tcu|website=ESPN|date=May 6, 2014}}</ref>

In 2015, he suffered a leg injury in the third game against [[Southern Methodist University]] and was given a [[Redshirt (college sports)|medical redshirt]]. As a senior in 2016, he started all 13 games at right tackle. He finished his college career after appearing in 49 games with 36 starts. He also practiced [[track and field]].

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Collins was the top performer at his position in the 2017 [[NFL Combine]]; his official 4.81-second [[40-yard dash]] is the third-fastest time ever by an offensive lineman, trailing only [[Terron Armstead]] (4.71 seconds) and [[Lane Johnson]] (4.72 seconds) on the all-time list. He also bench pressed 225 pounds 34 times, which tied for the second-best mark among all participants at the Combine.<ref>{{cite web|title=Aviante Collins Boasts Speed As Advantage, Runs Third Best 40 Time In History Of Combine For OL|date=March 3, 2017 |url=http://texashsfootball.com/aviante-collins-boasts-speed-advantage-runs-third-best-40-time-history-combine-ol/|publisher=NFL|access-date=May 3, 2018}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
Collins was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] after the [[2017 NFL draft]] on May 1, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Agree To Terms With 13 Rookie Free Agents|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-agree-to-terms-with-13-rookie-free-agents-18813122|website=Vikings.com|date=May 1, 2017|access-date=May 4, 2017}}</ref>

He competed with [[Jeremiah Sirles]], [[Reid Fragel]], and [[Rashod Hill]] to be a backup offensive tackle. Collins was named the third string right tackle behind starter [[Mike Remmers]] and backup [[Rashod Hill]] to begin the regular season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/198/MIN| title=Minnesota Vikings depth chart: 08/31/2017| access-date=October 2, 2017| website=ourlads.com}}</ref> As a rookie, he played in three games in a reserve role.

On September 10, 2018, Collins was placed on [[injured reserve]] with a torn biceps.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Sign G Bryan Witzmann, Place Aviante Collins on IR|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-sign-g-bryan-witzmann-place-aviante-collins-on-ir|website=Vikings.com|date=September 10, 2018}}</ref>

In 2019, he suffered a leg injury during training camp that limited his performance. On August 31, 2019, Collins was waived by the Vikings and was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves, Set Initial 53-Man Roster|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-2019-roster-cuts-53-man-roster|website=Vikings.com|date=August 31, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Fill Initial 2019 Practice Squad|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-practice-squad-2019|website=Vikings.com|date=September 1, 2019}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on November 14, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Sign Aviante Collins to Active Roster, Place Brett Jones on Reserve/Injured|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-sign-aviante-collins-to-active-roster-place-brett-jones-on-reserve-injur|website=Vikings.com|date=November 14, 2019}}</ref> He started in the season finale against the [[Chicago Bears]].

Collins was waived on September 5, 2020, and signed to the Vikings practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Peters |first1=Craig |last2=Smith |first2=Eric |title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves, Set Initial 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/2020-roster-53-man-announced |website=Minnesota Vikings |access-date=September 5, 2020 |date=September 5, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Claim LB Ryan Connelly, Add 13 Players To Practice Squad|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/ryan-connelly-2020-practice-squad-add-13-players|website=Vikings.com|date=September 6, 2020}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on November 21 for the team's week 11 game against the [[Dallas Cowboys]], and reverted to the practice squad after the game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Vikings Activate FB C.J. Ham, Announce Roster Moves |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-activate-fb-c-j-ham-announce-roster-moves |website=Vikings.com |date=November 21, 2020 |access-date=December 27, 2020}}</ref> His practice squad contract with the team expired after the season on January 11, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Five players have contracts expire |url=https://www.fantasyguru.com/vikings-five-players-have-contracts-expire/ |website=FantasyGuru.com |date=January 11, 2021 |access-date=February 17, 2021 |archive-date=January 18, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210118094552/https://www.fantasyguru.com/vikings-five-players-have-contracts-expire/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On February 2, 2021, Collins signed a reserve/futures contract with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Popejoy|first=Curt|date=February 2, 2021|title=Steelers sign OT Aviante Collins to Reserve/Future contract|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/steelers-sign-ot-aviante-collins-211216974.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210202213419/https://sports.yahoo.com/steelers-sign-ot-aviante-collins-211216974.html |archive-date=February 2, 2021 |access-date=2021-02-03|website=Yahoo Sports|language=en-US}}</ref> He was waived on August 24, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers reduce roster to 80|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-reduce-roster-to-80|website=Steelers.com|date=August 24, 2021}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On September 6, 2021, Collins was signed to the [[Dallas Cowboys]] practice squad.

He signed a reserve/future contract with the Cowboys on January 18, 2022. On August 30, 2022, Collins was waived by the Cowboys and signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys Make 28 Moves To Reach Roster Limit|url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-make-28-moves-to-reach-roster-limit|author=Eatman, Nick|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=August 30, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Rush, Grier & Maher Among Practice Squad Signees|url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/rush-grier-maher-among-practice-squad-signees|author=Eatman, Nick|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=August 31, 2022}}</ref> On November 23, 2022, he was elevated to the active roster from the practice squad. On December 3, 2022, he was elevated to the active roster from the practice squad. On December 10, 2022, he was elevated to the active roster from the practice squad. On January 16, 2023, he was elevated to the active roster from the practice squad. On January 21, 2023, he was promoted to the active roster for the NFC Divisional Playoffs game against the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. He wasn't re-signed after the season.

===Chicago Bears===
On July 26, 2023, Collins signed with the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-26 |title=Bears sign OT Aviante Collins, waive OT Lorenz Metz |url=https://bearswire.usatoday.com/2023/07/26/bears-roster-moves-aviante-collins-signed-lorenz-metz-waived/ |access-date=2023-07-26 |website=Bears Wire |language=en-US}}</ref> He was released on August 29, 2023, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite news|title=Roster Moves: Bears reach NFL's 53-man roster limit|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-reach-nfl-s-53-man-roster-limit-2023|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=August 29, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears sign 11 players to practice squad|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-sign-11-players-to-practice-squad|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=August 30, 2023}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 20.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears put Braxton Jones on IR|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-put-braxton-jones-on-ir|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=September 20, 2023}}</ref> He was released on October 29,<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaquan Brisker downgraded to out for Sunday night game vs. Chargers|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/jaquan-brisker-downgraded-to-out-for-sunday-night-game-vs-chargers|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=October 29, 2023}}</ref> but re-signed to their practice squad the following day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nfltraderumors.co/bears-re-sign-ol-aviante-collins-to-practice-squad/|work=NFLTradeRumors.co|title=Bears Re-sign OL Aviante Collins To Practice Squad|first=Nate|last=Broude|date=October 30, 2023}}</ref> He appeared in one game as a backup offensive tackle.

Collins signed a reserve/future contract on January 8, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears sign 10 to reserve/future contracts|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-sign-10-to-reserve-future-contracts-2024|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=January 8, 2024}}</ref> He was released on August 27.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears reach 53-man roster limit|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-reach-53-man-roster-limit-2024|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His father, [[Bill Collins (athlete)|Bill]], was a notable sprinter at TCU, who won two Southwest Conference titles in the [[100 metres]] in 1974 and 1975. He was inducted into the TCU Letterwinners Association Hall of Fame. His mother, Robin Stephens, received [[All-American]] honors at the [[University of Houston]] in 1984.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McClain |first=John |author-link=John McClain |date=March 3, 2017 |title=Willowridge product Aviante Collins shines at combine |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/texans/article/Willowridge-product-Aviante-Collins-shines-at-10975753.php |access-date=2024-07-06 |website=Chron.com}}</ref>

'''Austin Traylor''' (born September 3, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin Badgers]].

==Early life==
Traylor attended [[Walnut Ridge High School (Columbus, Ohio)|Walnut Ridge High School]]. He accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].

==Professional career==
===Dallas Cowboys===
Traylor was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] after the [[2016 NFL draft]] on May 17.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys Sign Workout Invite TE Austin Traylor To 90-Man Roster|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/05/17/cowboys-sign-workout-invite-te-austin-traylor-90-man-roster|author=Helman, David|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=May 17, 2016|accessdate=December 9, 2017}}</ref> He was waived on September 3, 2016, and signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Three Former Draft Picks Among Cowboys' Cuts; McFadden Moved To NFI|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/09/03/three-former-draft-picks-among-cowboys-cuts-mcfadden-moved-nfi|author=Helman, David|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=September 3, 2016|accessdate=December 9, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180222185931/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/09/03/three-former-draft-picks-among-cowboys-cuts-mcfadden-moved-nfi|archivedate=February 22, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys Sign Sanchez, Release Showers; 7 Added To Practice Squad|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/09/04/cowboys-sign-sanchez-release-showers-7-added-practice-squad|author=Helman, David|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=September 4, 2016|accessdate=December 9, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170815024810/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/09/04/cowboys-sign-sanchez-release-showers-7-added-practice-squad|archivedate=August 15, 2017}}</ref> He was released on September 14.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cowboys Sign Veteran Defensive End Davis For Pass Rush Depth|url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/09/14/cowboys-sign-veteran-defensive-end-davis-pass-rush-depth?sf35902697=1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160915110001/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/09/14/cowboys-sign-veteran-defensive-end-davis-pass-rush-depth?sf35902697=1|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 15, 2016|author=Phillips, Rob|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=September 14, 2016|accessdate=December 9, 2017}}</ref>

===San Diego Chargers===
On September 20, 2016, Traylor was signed to the [[San Diego Chargers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chargers Sign Versatile RB Dexter McCluster|url=http://www.chargers.com/news/2016/09/20/chargers-sign-versatile-rb-dexter-mccluster|author=Henne, Ricky|website=Chargers.com|date=September 20, 2016|accessdate=December 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160922125101/http://www.chargers.com/news/2016/09/20/chargers-sign-versatile-rb-dexter-mccluster|archive-date=September 22, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was released on October 4, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bolts Add Trio to Practice Squad|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/bolts-add-trio-to-practice-squad-139016|author=Henne, Ricky|website=Chargers.com|date=October 4, 2016|accessdate=December 9, 2017}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On November 1, 2016, Traylor was signed to the [[New England Patriots]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots sign OL Chase Farris and Austin Traylor to the practice squad|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-ol-chase-farris-and-austin-traylor-to-the-practice-squad-277856|website=Patriots.com|date=November 1, 2016|accessdate=December 9, 2017}}</ref> He was released on November 12, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots activate Dion Lewis to 53-man roster; Make practice squad transactions|url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2016/11/12/patriots-activate-dion-lewis-53-man-roster-make-practice-squad-transactions|website=Patriots.com|date=November 12, 2016|accessdate=December 9, 2017}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On November 15, 2016, Traylor was signed to the [[Baltimore Ravens]]' practice squad, but was released four days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Promote Asa Jackson, Place DT Willie Henry on Injured Reserve|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Promote-DB-Asa-Jackson-Place-DT-Willie-Henry-On-Injured-Reserve/1e6c3934-be9b-43bc-abca-9953be8a0500|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171112170211/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Promote-DB-Asa-Jackson-Place-DT-Willie-Henry-On-Injured-Reserve/1e6c3934-be9b-43bc-abca-9953be8a0500|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 12, 2017|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=November 15, 2016|accessdate=December 9, 2017}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
On December 20, 2016, Traylor was signed to the [[Denver Broncos]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Broncos sign TE Austin Traylor to practice squad|url=https://247sports.com/nfl/denver-broncos/article/report-broncos-sign-te-austin-traylor-to-practice-squad-49951538/|website=247sports.com|date=December 21, 2016|access-date=December 9, 2017}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Broncos on January 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos sign 11 players to future contracts|url=http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-sign-11-players-to-future-contracts/1a1be5de-6e71-44a1-b1cf-740f071481b4|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128093028/http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-sign-11-players-to-future-contracts/1a1be5de-6e71-44a1-b1cf-740f071481b4|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 28, 2018|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=January 2, 2017|accessdate=December 9, 2017}}</ref>

On September 2, 2017, Traylor was waived by the Broncos and was signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos trim roster at deadline|url=http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-trim-roster-at-deadline/234c49ac-2b09-496b-9175-b8fdc28f39dd|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171130182211/http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-trim-roster-at-deadline/234c49ac-2b09-496b-9175-b8fdc28f39dd|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 30, 2017|author=Mason, Andrew|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=September 2, 2017|accessdate=December 9, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos announce initial practice-squad roster|url=http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-announce-initial-practice-squad-roster/a612ad8b-44a1-49b7-801a-a4ee46bb39bb|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180210213128/http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-announce-initial-practice-squad-roster/a612ad8b-44a1-49b7-801a-a4ee46bb39bb|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 10, 2018|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=September 4, 2017|accessdate=December 9, 2017}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on November 18, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos promote TE Austin Traylor to active roster, designate A.J. Derby waived/injured|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-promote-te-austin-traylor-to-active-roster-designate-a-j-derby--19791702|author=Swanson, Ben|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=November 18, 2017|accessdate=December 9, 2017}}</ref>

===Salt Lake Stallions===
In January [[2019 AAF season|2019]], Traylor joined the [[Salt Lake Stallions]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Heath|first=Jon|url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/2019/01/15/rahim-moore-among-former-denver-broncos-joining-aaf-football-league/|title=Rahim Moore among former Broncos joining new AAF league|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|publisher=Broncos Wire|date=January 15, 2019|accessdate=February 5, 2019}}</ref> He caught 2 passes for 12 yards in 8 games played,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://noextrapoints.com/players/austin-traylor/|title = Austin Traylor}}</ref> after which the league shut down in April.

===Detroit Lions===
On July 22, 2019, Traylor signed with the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions sign free agent TE Austin Traylor|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-sign-free-agent-te-austin-traylor|website=DetroitLions.com|date=July 22, 2019}}</ref> He was waived on August 31, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Detroit Lions establish 53-man roster|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/detroit-lions-establish-53-man-roster|website=DetroitLions.com|date=August 31, 2019}}</ref>

'''Bobby Gene Hill Jr.''' (born April 20, 1995) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive tackle]] for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[NC State Wolfpack football|NC State Wolfpack]] and was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the third round of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Valentine |first=Ed |date=2018-04-27 |title=Giants 2018 draft: DT B.J. Hill is selected 69th overall by New York Giants |url=https://www.bigblueview.com/2018/4/27/17293110/giants-2018-draft-dt-b-j-hill-is-selected-69th-overall-by-new-york-giants |access-date=2022-02-06 |website=Big Blue View |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Along with [[high school football|football]], Hill participated in track and field, baseball, and basketball at [[West Stanly High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=All-Time Roster – West Stanly Colts Football (Oakboro, NC) |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/high-schools/west-stanly-colts-(oakboro,nc)/football/all_time_roster.htm |access-date=August 18, 2018 |website=www.maxpreps.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=BJ Hill |url=https://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/Athlete.aspx?AID=2005067 |access-date=August 18, 2018 |website=Athletic.net |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=All-Time Roster – West Stanly Colts Basketball (Oakboro, NC) |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/high-schools/west-stanly-colts-(oakboro,nc)/basketball/all_time_roster.htm |access-date=August 18, 2018 |website=www.maxpreps.com |language=en}}</ref> As a senior, Hill recorded nine sacks, an interception, and five rushing touchdowns, playing both defensive end and running back.<ref> https://www.bengals.com/team/players-roster/b-j-hill/career </ref> He was listed as a three-star defensive end recruit by [[247Sports.com]] and committed to [[North Carolina State University|NC State]] on June 12, 2013, to play football, over offers from [[East Carolina Pirates football|East Carolina]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=B.J. Hill, West Stanly , Strong-Side Defensive End |url=https://247sports.com/Player/BJ-Hill-21905?Institution=17289 |access-date=August 18, 2018 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Muma |first=Steven |date=June 12, 2013 |title=NCSU Picks Up Two Commitments |url=https://www.backingthepack.com/2013/6/12/4425210/b-j-hill-kalen-mccain-commit-nc-state-football |access-date=September 21, 2020 |website=Backing The Pack |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Hill attended and played [[college football]] at NC State from 2014 to 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=B.J. Hill College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bj-hill-3.html |access-date=October 18, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He became a starting defensive tackle midway through his freshman year, and maintained his starting role for his entire college career, playing in 51 games with 44 starts. He ended his career with 187 tackles, nine sacks, two forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, and 10 pass deflections.<ref> https://www.bengals.com/team/players-roster/b-j-hill/career</ref> He was named Honorable Mention All-ACC for his senior season in 2017, recording 57 tackles, three sacks, and a forced fumble. His success led to him being invited to play in the 2018 [[Senior Bowl]].<ref> https://www.giants.com/news/giants-draft-nc-state-dt-b-j-hill-at-no-69-20598837#:~:text=In%20his%20final%20season%2C%20Hill,invite%20to%20the%20Senior%20Bow.</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
On December 4, 2017, it was announced that Hill had accepted his invitation to play in the [[2018 Senior Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bradham |first=Matthew |date=December 4, 2018 |title=NC State DT BJ Hill Accepts Invitation to Play In Senior Bowl |url=https://packinsider.com/2017/12/04/nc-state-dt-bj-hill-accepts-invitation-play-senior-bowl/ |access-date=August 25, 2018 |website=packinsider.com}}</ref> Hill was dominant during [[Senior Bowl]] practices and impressed scouts and team representatives.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peterson |first=Michael |date=February 2, 2018 |title=7 Round Mock Draft: Senior Bowl Roster Edition |url=https://www.boltsfromtheblue.com/2018/2/2/16959822/los-angeles-chargers-7-round-mock-draft-senior-bowl-roster-edition |access-date=August 25, 2018 |website=boltsfromtheblue.com}}</ref> On January 27, 2018, Hill played in the 2018 Reese's Senior Bowl and was part of [[Denver Broncos|Denver Broncos']] head coach [[Vance Joseph|Vance Joseph's]] North team that lost to the South 45–16. He attended the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] in [[Indianapolis]] and completed all of the combine and positional drills. Hill's overall performance helped raise his draft stock, as he finished third among all defensive linemen in the bench press, fifth in the three-cone drill, tied for 11th in the 20-yard shuttle, and finished 15th among his position group in the 40-yard dash.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 NFL Scouting Combine: Top Performers: 40-yard dash (defensive lineman) |url=https://www.nfl.com/combine/top-performers |access-date=August 25, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On March 19, 2018, Hill participated at NC State's pro day, but opted to stand on his combine numbers and only performed positional drills. Hill also attended a pre-draft visits with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] and [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rutter, Joe |date=April 16, 2018 |title=Steelers host defensive line draft prospects Gilmore, Nichols |url=https://triblive.com/sports/steelers/13542583-74/steelers-host-defensive-line-draft-prospects-gilmore-nichols |access-date=August 25, 2018 |website=triblive.com}}</ref> At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, Hill was projected to be a second or third round pick by NFL draft experts and scouts. He was ranked as the fifth best defensive tackle prospect in the draft by [[Scouts Inc.]] and was ranked the seventh best defensive tackle by DraftScout.com.<ref>{{Cite web |title=B.J. Hill, DS #7 DT, North Carolina State |url=http://www.draftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=132904&draftyear=2018&genpos=dt |access-date=August 25, 2018 |website=DraftScout.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL B.J. Hill -ESPN |url=http://espn.com/nfldraftcard?playerId=101722& |access-date=August 25, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}{{Dead link|date=October 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

=== New York Giants===
The [[New York Giants]] selected Hill in the third round with the 69th overall pick in the [[2018 NFL draft]]. Hill was the fifth defensive tackle drafted in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2018/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-17 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The pick used to select Hill was acquired from the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in exchange for [[Jason Pierre-Paul]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salomone |first=Dan |date=April 27, 2018 |title=Giants draft NC State DT B.J. Hill at No. 69 |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-draft-NC-State-DT-BJ-Hill-at-No-69/d47e5532-fb15-41ed-ad6e-407ebb15e918 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180512043917/https://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-draft-NC-State-DT-BJ-Hill-at-No-69/d47e5532-fb15-41ed-ad6e-407ebb15e918 |archive-date=May 12, 2018 |access-date=May 10, 2018 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> On June 7, 2018, the Giants signed Hill to a four-year, $4.04 million contract that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $1.02 million.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: B.J. Hill contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/new-york-giants/b.j.-hill-25168/ |access-date=August 24, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref> In Week 3, against the [[Houston Texans]], he recorded his first career sack.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rock |first=Tom |date=September 23, 2018 |title=Giants' defense pulls the plug on Texans |url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/football/giants/giants-texans-1.21228701 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181010012703/https://www.newsday.com/sports/football/giants/giants-texans-1.21228701 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 10, 2018 |access-date=October 9, 2018 |website=Newsday |language=en}}</ref> In the next game, a loss to the [[New Orleans Saints]], he recorded his second sack of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trahan |first=Ken |date=September 30, 2018 |title=Saints run away from Giants for 33–18 win |url=https://crescentcitysports.com/saints-run-away-from-giants-for-33-18-win/ |access-date=October 18, 2018 |website=Crescent City Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
On August 30, 2021, Hill was traded to the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] for center [[Billy Price (American football)|Billy Price]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salomone |first=Dan |date=August 30, 2021 |title=Giants to trade DL B.J. Hill; details not finalized |url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-to-trade-dl-b-j-hill-details-not-finalized-joe-judge |website=Giants.com |accessdate=August 30, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hobson |first=Geoff |date=August 30, 2021 |title=Price For Trade As Bengals Pick Up D-Tackle From Giants |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/price-for-trade-as-bengals-pick-up-d-tackle-from-giants |website=Bengals.com |accessdate=August 30, 2021}}</ref> In the [[2021–22_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Cincinnati_Bengals_27,_Kansas_City_Chiefs_24_(OT)|AFC Championship]] against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], he intercepted [[Patrick Mahomes II|Patrick Mahomes]] when the Bengals were down 13–21 with 2:18 remaining in the third quarter, leading to the game-tying touchdown in the eventual 27–24 overtime victory.<ref name="202201300kan">{{Cite web |title=AFC Championship – Cincinnati Bengals at Kansas City Chiefs – January 30th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201300kan.htm |access-date=February 6, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 15, 2022, Hill signed a three-year, $30 million contract extension with the Bengals.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals Re-Sign B.J. Hill|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-re-sign-b-j-hill|website=Bengals.com|date=March 15, 2022|access-date=March 16, 2022}}</ref> He finished the 2022 season with three sacks, 68 tackles, four passes defended, one forced fumble, and three fumble recoveries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=B.J. Hill 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HillB.00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2025-01-19 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 12, 2025, Hill signed a three-year, $33 million contract extension with the Bengals.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals Re-sign DT B.J. Hill|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-resign-dt-bj-hill-bengals-roster-update|website=Bengals.com|date=March 12, 2025}}</ref>

'''Avonte Michael Maddox''' (born March 31, 1996)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://pittsburghpanthers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1156|title=Avonte Maddox - 2015 Football Roster - University of Pittsburgh|website=pittsburghpanthers.com|language=en|access-date=April 28, 2018}}</ref> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[Detroit Lions]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]].

== Early life ==
After playing little league football, Maddox focused on [[baseball]] his first two years of high school before switching to [[high school football|football]]. He received only two [[Power Five conferences|Power Five]] scholarship offers, one from [[Purdue Boilermakers football|Purdue]] and one from [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Batko |first=Brian |date=March 26, 2018 |title=How Avonte Maddox went from MLB to NFL draft hopeful |url=http://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2018/03/26/avonte-maddox-nfl-draft-projection-pitt-panthers-baseball-football-pittsburgh-pat-narduzzi-cornerback/stories/201803250087 |access-date=April 28, 2018 |work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |language=en}}</ref> He was also nearly drafted into the [[MLB]] after his senior year of high school.<ref name=":2" />

== College career ==
[[File:Avonte Maddox (151228-D-DB155-009) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Maddox with Pitt at the [[2015 Military Bowl]]]]
Maddox started at [[cornerback]] all four years at Pitt.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Batko |first=Brian |date=November 25, 2017 |title=Avonte Maddox symbolizes a super sendoff for Pitt seniors |url=http://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2017/11/25/avonte-maddox-pitt-football-senior-day-2017-pittsburgh-panthers-miami-nathan-bossory-devon-edwards/stories/201711250097 |access-date=April 28, 2018 |website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |language=en}}</ref> He was named Honorable Mention All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] his sophomore year and Second-team his senior year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.draftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=1006176&draftyear=2018&genpos=CB|title=Avonte Maddox {{!}} Pittsburgh, CB : 2018 NFL Draft Scout Player Profile|website=www.draftscout.com|access-date=April 28, 2018}}</ref> Maddox missed two games in both his junior and senior years due to injury.<ref name=":0" />

===Philadelphia Eagles===
Maddox was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the fourth round (125th overall) of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gowton |first=Brandon Lee |date=April 28, 2018 |title=NFL Draft Results: Eagles pick Avonte Maddox at No. 125 |url=https://www.bleedinggreennation.com/2018/4/28/17295888/nfl-draft-results-eagles-pick-avonte-maddox-no-125-slot-nickel-pittsburgh-philadelphia-defense |access-date=July 4, 2018 |website=Bleeding Green Nation|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> He made his NFL debut during the league season opener on September 6, 2018, against the [[Atlanta Falcons]], playing on [[special teams]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809060phi.htm#all_vis_snap_counts|title=Atlanta Falcons at Philadelphia Eagles - September 6th, 2018-Snap counts|publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=September 30, 2018}}</ref> Maddox recorded his first career interception by picking off a pass from [[Tennessee Titans]]' quarterback [[Marcus Mariota]] in a 26–23 overtime loss on September 30.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bleedinggreennation.com/2018/9/30/17920552/philadelpiha-eagles-rookie-avonte-maddox-first-career-interception-week-4-titans-video-replay-watch|title=Eagles rookie Avonte Maddox gets first career interception against the Titans|first=Alexis|last=Chassen|work=Bleeding Green Nation|publisher=SBNation.com|date=September 30, 2018|access-date=September 30, 2018}}</ref> He recorded his second interception of the season off of quarterback [[Jared Goff]] during the 30–23 win over the [[Los Angeles Rams]].

On September 26, 2019, late in a game against the [[Green Bay Packers]], Maddox collided helmets with teammate [[Andrew Sendejo]] on an attempted tackle of [[Jamaal Williams]] and had to be carted off the field on a stretcher. The Eagles announced that Maddox had movement in all of his extremities, but was taken to a local hospital overnight as a precaution and for further evaluation; he returned with the team the next day.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2019/09/27/avonte-maddox-carted-off-eagles-packers |title=Eagles CB Avonte Maddox Carted Off Late in Thursday Night Win Over Packers |last=Rollins |first=Khadrice |date=September 27, 2019 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=September 27, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2019/09/27/avonte-maddox-eagles-injury-updates-packers |title=Report: Eagles' Avonte Maddox Flies Home With Team After Huge Hit |last= Carroll |first=Charlotte |date=September 27, 2019 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=September 27, 2019}}</ref>

In the 2020 season, during the Eagles' Week 3 game against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], Maddox suffered an injury which ultimately forced him to miss the next three games before being re-activated on Week 7. On December 18, 2020, Maddox was placed on season-ending [[Injured reserve list|injured reserve]] after suffering a knee injury in a Week 14 win over the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles place T Jack Driscoll, CB Avonte Maddox on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-place-jack-driscoll-avonte-maddox-on-injured-reserve|author=McPherson, Chris|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=December 18, 2020}}</ref> He finished the season with 40 tackles and three pass deflections, playing in 10 games with eight starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Avonte Maddox 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MaddAv00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=January 1, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Starting the last season of his rookie contract in 2021, Maddox led the Eagles in tackles (9) during their 32–6 win over the [[Atlanta Falcons]]. On October 24 against the [[Las Vegas Raiders]], Maddox recorded his third career interception during the 33–22 loss.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MaddAv00/gamelog/|title= Pro Football Reference: Avonte Maddox Game Logs}}</ref> On November 20, 2021, Maddox signed a three-year, $22.5 million contract extension with the Eagles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clancy |first=Shamus  |date=November 20, 2021 |title=Avonte Maddox, Eagles agree to three-year contract extension |url=https://www.bleedinggreennation.com/2021/11/20/22793132/avonte-maddox-eagles-agree-three-year-contract-extension-2018-nfl-draft-howie-roseman-deal-bgn |access-date=June 14, 2025 |website=Bleeding Green Nation |publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> He was placed on the COVID list on January 3, 2022.<ref>{{cite news |title=Eagles place 12 players on Reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-place-12-players-on-reserve-covid-19-list |author=Oddo, Jillian |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |date=January 3, 2022}}</ref> Maddox was activated one week later on January 10, missing just one game in which the Eagles did not use their starters.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles Clear COVID List, Place Three on IR|url=https://www.sportstalkphilly.com/2022/01/eagles-clear-covid-list-place-three-on-ir.html|author=Bowman, Paul|website=SportsTalkPhilly.com|date=January 10, 2022}}</ref>

Maddox returned as a starter in 2022 as the team's primary nickelback. He was placed on injured reserve on November 14, 2022, with a [[hamstring]] injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McPherson |first=Chris |date=November 14, 2022 |title=Eagles place CB Avonte Maddox on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-place-avonte-maddox-on-injured-reserve-chase-young |access-date=March 26, 2023 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> He was activated on December 10. On December 26, it was announced that Maddox had suffered a 'significant' toe injury and would miss the remainder of the regular season.<ref name="m008">{{cite web | last=Frank | first=Reuben | title=Avonte Maddox reportedly has serious toe injury | website=NBC Sports - Philadelphia | date=December 26, 2022 | url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nfl/philadelphia-eagles/avonte-maddox-reportedly-has-serious-toe-injury/265230/?amp=1 | access-date=September 23, 2024}}</ref> Maddox reached [[Super Bowl LVII]] where the Eagles lost 38–35 to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]]; he recorded seven tackles in the game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LVII - Philadelphia Eagles vs. Kansas City Chiefs - February 12th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202302120phi.htm |access-date=March 26, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On September 20, 2023, Maddox was placed on injured reserve after suffering a pec injury in Week 2.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McPherson |first=Chris |date=September 20, 2023 |title=Eagles make several roster moves |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-roster-moves-britain-covey-avonte-maddox-bryant-koback |access-date=October 31, 2024 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> He was activated on December 30.<ref name="u659">{{cite web | last=Boyle | first=Owen | title=Eagles activate Avonte Maddox from Injured Reserve | website=Philadelphia Eagles | date=December 30, 2023 | url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-activate-avonte-maddox-from-injured-reserve | access-date=September 23, 2024}}</ref>

On March 7, 2024, Maddox was released by the Eagles.<ref name="a571">{{cite web | last=Frank | first=Reuben | title=Eagles release cornerback Avonte Maddox after six seasons | website=NBC Sports Philadelphia | date=March 6, 2024 | url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nfl/philadelphia-eagles/eagles-release-cornerback-avonte-maddox-after-six-seasons/569442/ | access-date=October 19, 2024}}</ref><ref name="a638">{{cite web | last=McPherson | first=Chris | title=Eagles release Avonte Maddox | website=Philadelphia Eagles | date=March 7, 2024 | url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-release-avonte-maddox | access-date=September 23, 2024}}</ref> He re-signed with the team on April 4.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spadaro |first=Dave |date=April 4, 2024 |title=Eagles sign Avonte Maddox to a 1-year contract |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-sign-avonte-maddox |access-date=October 31, 2024 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> Maddox won his first Super Bowl when the Eagles defeated the [[2024 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]] 40–22 in [[Super Bowl LIX]]. Maddox had one pass defended in the game, forcing a turnover on downs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LIX - Kansas City Chiefs at Philadelphia Eagles - February 9th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202502090phi.htm |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
On March 21, 2025, Maddox signed a one-year contract with his hometown team, the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 21, 2025 |title=Detroit Lions sign unrestricted free agent CB Avonte Maddox |url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-sign-unrestricted-free-agent-cb-avonte-maddox |access-date=2025-08-20 |website=DetroitLions.com}}</ref> 

On April 6, 2026, Maddox signed another one-year contract with the Lions.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 6, 2026 |title=Detroit Lions bolster secondary depth by re-signing veteran defender |url=https://www.mlive.com/lions/2026/04/detroit-lions-bolster-secondary-depth-by-re-signing-veteran-defender.html |access-date=2026-04-06 |website=mlive.com}}</ref>

'''Azeem Victor''' (born September 19, 1995) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Washington Huskies football|Washington]].

==College career==
He played [[college football]] for [[Washington Huskies football|Washington]]. Victor was a first-team all-[[Pac-12 Conference]] selection in 2016 after posting 67 [[tackled gridiron|tackles]] but missed the last month with a broken tibia. Going into the 2017 season, Victor was an [[Associated Press]] preseason first-team [[All-American]]. His season ended in November after he was suspended by coach [[Chris Petersen]] for a DUI charge.<ref>{{cite web | last=Bonagura | first=Kyle | title=Washington LB Victor suspended after arrest | website=ESPN.com | date=2017-11-15 | url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/21426490/azeem-victor-washington-huskies-suspended-dui-arrest | access-date=2025-07-05}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Victor was selected by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the sixth round (216th overall) of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cockerham |first=Carl |date=April 28, 2018 |title=2018 NFL Draft results: With pick 216 in 6th round Raiders select Washington LB Azeem Victor |url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/2018/4/28/17296784/2018-nfl-draft-results-with-pick-216-in-6th-round-raiders-select-washington-lb-azeem-victor |access-date=July 3, 2018 |website=SilverAndBlackPride.com}}</ref> He was waived on September 1, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Oakland Raiders announce roster transactions – 9.1.18|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/oakland-raiders-announce-roster-transactions-2|website=Raiders.com|date=September 1, 2018}}</ref>

On September 3, 2018, Victor was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bobo Wilson Returns on First Practice Squad|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bobo-wilson-returns-on-first-practice-squad|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=September 2, 2018}}</ref> He was released on September 11, 2018.<ref>{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=September 11, 2018 |title=Bucs Add CB Marcus Williams, Release G Adam Gettis |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-add-cb-marcus-williams-release-g-adam-gettis |access-date=February 23, 2026 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref>

On September 26, 2018, Victor was signed to the [[Seattle Seahawks]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patton |first=Andy |date=September 26, 2018 |title=Seahawks sign linebacker Azeem Victor to practice squad |url=https://seahawkswire.usatoday.com/2018/09/26/seahawks-sign-linebacker-azeem-victor-to-practice-squad/ |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Seahawks Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref> He was released on October 23, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patton |first=Andy |date=October 23, 2018 |title=Seahawks add Justin Currie, J.J. Dielman to practice squad |url=https://seahawkswire.usatoday.com/2018/10/23/seahawks-add-justin-currie-j-j-dielman-to-practice-squad/ |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Seahawks Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

In 2019, Victor joined the [[Orlando Apollos]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/orlando-apollos-set-final-roster/n-5442986|title=Orlando Apollos Set Final Roster|work=Our Sports Central|date=January 30, 2019|access-date=February 6, 2019}}</ref> He played in four games for the Apollos, recording one assisted tackle. He was waived on March 12, 2019.<ref name="Sc"/>

Victor was suspended for the first 10 weeks of the [[2019 NFL season]] on April 24, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |author=Levine, Ben |title=LB Azeem Victor Suspended 10 Games |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2019/04/free-agent-lb-azeem-victor-suspended-10-games |website=ProFootballRumors.com |date=April 24, 2019 |access-date=November 4, 2019}}</ref> He was reinstated from suspension on November 12, 2019.

He played in one game for the [[Calgary Stampeders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] in 2019, totaling one defensive tackle and one special teams tackle.<ref name="Sc"/>

Victor signed with the Alphas of [[The Spring League]] in May 2021.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=TheSpringLeague |title=First look at the #TSLAlphas roster at #TSL2021! |number=1389019179743858688 |date=May 2, 2021 |access-date=June 22, 2021}}</ref>

Victor was selected by the [[Houston Gamblers (2022)|Houston Gamblers]] of the [[USFL (2022)|United States Football league]] (USFL) in the 29th round of the [[2022 USFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/news/usfl-draft-2022-picks-results-rosters/kfjtmrpdeztksutjassswllz|website=[[Sporting News]]|title=USFL Draft tracker: Complete results, rosters for new football league|date=February 23, 2022|author=Camenker, Jacob}}</ref> He played in five games for the Gamblers in 2022, recording ten solo tackles and seven assisted tackles.<ref name="Sc">{{cite web | url=https://www.statscrew.com/football/stats/p-victoaze001 | title=Azeem Victor | publisher=statscrew.com | accessdate=9 November 2024}}</ref><ref name="pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/v/vict00050.html | title=Azeem Victor | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=9 November 2024}}</ref> He was released on May 20, 2022.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLGamblers |title=Roster Updates |number=1527546510220464129 |date=May 20, 2022 |access-date=May 23, 2022}}</ref>

==Coaching career==

Victor signed with Athletes Untapped as a private football coach on Mar 21, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Press Release: Private Football Coaching with Azeem Victor |url=https://athletesuntapped.com/blog/football-lessons-with-azeem-victor/ |website=athletesuntapped.com |publisher=Athletes Untapped |date=Mar 21, 2024 |access-date=October 31, 2025}}</ref>

'''Austin Rashad Walter''' (born August 17, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Rice Owls football|Rice Owls]].

== College career ==
Walter played college football at [[Rice Owls football|Rice]], where he rushed for 1,744 yards and 13 touchdowns, averaging 5.1 yards per carry; he also had 79 receptions for 803 yards, and in his senior season, averaged 27.3 yards on 18 kickoff returns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=49ers sign undrafted Rice running back Austin Walter after tryout |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/49ers-sign-undrafted-rice-running-153130779.html |access-date=June 4, 2019 |website=sports.yahoo.com |archive-date=June 4, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190604145955/https://sports.yahoo.com/49ers-sign-undrafted-rice-running-153130779.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Professional career ==
===San Francisco 49ers (first stint)===
Walter went undrafted in the [[2019 NFL draft]]. He signed with the [[San Francisco 49ers]] on May 4, 2019, after a tryout with the team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Walter on Instagram: "I've been playing this game since I was 3 years old and today I finally made my dreams come true. I reached the highest level of…" |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BxDgSwjhsd3/  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/BxDgSwjhsd3 |archive-date=December 24, 2021 |url-access=registration|access-date=June 4, 2019 |website=Instagram |language=en}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 5, 2019 |title=49ers sign undrafted Rice RB Austin Walter after tryout |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/49ers/49ers-sign-undrafted-rice-running-back-austin-walter-after-tryout |access-date=June 4, 2019 |website=NBCS Bay Area}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Posey |first=Kyle |date=May 5, 2019 |title=49ers sign RB Austin Walter after tryout |url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2019/5/5/18530355/49ers-sign-rb-austin-walter-after-tryout-rookie-minicamp |access-date=June 4, 2019 |website=Niners Nation}}</ref> He was waived by the 49ers on August 31, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 31, 2019 |title=49ers Announce 53-man Roster |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-53-man-roster |website=49ers.com}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On September 18, 2019, Walter was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 18, 2019 |title=Giants sign RB Austin Walter to practice squad, release TE C.J. Conrad |url=https://giantswire.usatoday.com/2019/09/18/new-york-giants-sign-austin-walter-practice-squad-release-cj-conrad/ |website=Giants Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref> Following injuries to starting running back [[Saquon Barkley]] and backup [[Wayne Gallman]], Walter was promoted to the 53-man roster on October 10, 2019, but then waived the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 10, 2019 |title=Giants waive QB Alex Tanney, promote RB Austin Walter before TNF matchup with Patriots |url=https://www.sny.tv/giants/news/giants-waive-qb-alex-tanney-promote-rb-austin-walter-before-tnf-matchup-with-patriots/311122660 |website=SNY}}</ref>

===New York Jets===

Walter was re-signed to the practice squad on October 5, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Place LB Hamsah Nasirildeen on IR, Sign OL Isaiah Williams|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-lb-hamsah-nasirildeen-on-ir-sign-ol-isaiah-williams|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=October 5, 2021}}</ref>  Walter played his first game for the Jets against the [[Houston Texans]] on November 28, 2021, and rushed for 38 yards on 9 carries, including his first NFL touchdown.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ready for His Moment|author=Cannizzaro, Mark|pages=50–51|newspaper=New York Post|date=November 29, 2021|accessdate=2021-11-29|url=https://nypost.com/2021/11/29/journeyman-austin-walter-has-his-jets-prayers-answered/}}</ref> On December 4, 2021, Walter was elevated from the practice squad for the game against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign K Alex Kessman to Active Roster, Release K Matt Ammendola|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-k-alex-kessman-to-active-roster-release-k-matt-ammendola|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=newyorkjets.com|date=December 4, 2021|access-date=December 5, 2021|archive-date=December 5, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211205003508/https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-k-alex-kessman-to-active-roster-release-k-matt-ammendola|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 7, 2021, Walter was promoted to the active roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign RB Austin Walter, Place WR Corey Davis on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-wr-corey-davis-on-injured-reserve-release-s-jarrod-wilson|author= Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=December 7, 2021}}</ref> He was waived on May 6, 2022.

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On July 29, 2022, Walter signed with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders sign RB Austin Walter|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-running-back-austin-walter-2022-nfl-training-camp|website=Raiders.com|date=July 29, 2022|access-date=July 31, 2022|archive-date=July 31, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220731083008/https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-running-back-austin-walter-2022-nfl-training-camp|url-status=dead}}</ref> A few days later, in the 2022 [[Pro Football Hall of Fame Game|Pro Football Hall of Fame game]], Walter scored a touchdown against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap/_/gameId/401437964|title=Raiders give McDaniels happy homecoming, beat Jaguars 27-11 |author=AP |website=ESPN.com |date=August 5, 2022 |access-date=September 2, 2022}}</ref> On August 30, 2022, Walter was waived by the Raiders<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-finalize-initial-53-man-roster-2022-season-transactions-waive-release|title=Raiders finalize initial 53-man roster for the 2022 season|website=Raiders.com|date=August 30, 2022|access-date=August 30, 2022}}</ref> and then signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-announce-2022-practice-squad-additions-nfl-transactions-roster|title=Raiders announce practice squad additions|website=Raiders.com|date=August 31, 2022 |access-date=September 2, 2022}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 9, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders sign 13 players to Reserve/Future contracts|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-13-players-to-reserve-future-contracts-nfl-transactions-2023|website=Raiders.com|date=January 9, 2023}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 3, 2023.

'''Azeez Al-Shaair''' ({{IPAc-en|æ|l|ˈ|ʃ|aɪər}} {{respell|al|SHIRE}}, [[Arabic]]: عزيز الشاعر, born August 4, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Houston Texans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Atlantic Owls football|Florida Atlantic Owls]], where he received First-team All C-USA in [[2017 Conference USA football season#Postseason awards|2017]].

==Early life==
Al-Shaair was born in [[Tampa, Florida]]. As a young child, he moved back and forth between Tampa and [[Saudi Arabia]], where his father worked as an English instructor, but would stop living there after his parents divorced. He lived in [[Section 8 (housing)|Section 8]] housing and became homeless as a sophomore in high school after his home burned down. He commuted two hours by bus from a motel to [[Hillsborough High School (Tampa, Florida)|Hillsborough High School]], where he played [[high school football|football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Habib |first=Hal |date=August 29, 2018 |title=Faith fuels FAU linebacker Al-Shaair's rise toward stardom, NFL future |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/sports/college-football/faith-fuels-fau-linebacker-shaair-rise-toward-stardom-nfl-future/umNi1RO1xp6j9oOJddaYMJ/ |access-date=May 7, 2020 |work=[[Palm Beach Post]]}}</ref> As a senior, he made 126 tackles with 6.5 sacks, two interceptions, three forced fumbles and three fumble recoveries and also blocked six field goals and a blocked punt and was named first-team All-County.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Nate |date=February 2, 2015 |title=Meet the Owls' 2015 commits: Bios, highlights of prospects set to sign with FAU |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/fau-owls/sfl-meet-fau-commits-20150202-story.html |access-date=May 7, 2020 |work=[[Sun-Sentinel]]}}</ref> Al-Shaair committed to play [[college football]] at [[Florida Atlantic University]] going into his senior year, but continued to go on recruiting visits in order to help feed his family.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wolken |first=Dan |date=January 29, 2020 |title=Through teenage homelessness, 49ers' Azeez Al-Shaair kept NFL dream alive |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/super-bowl/2020/01/29/azeez-al-shaair-niners-super-bowl-florida-atlantic/4601386002/ |access-date=May 7, 2020 |work=[[USA Today]]}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:2018-0719-CUSAMD-Aziz Al-Shaair.JPG|thumb|left|upright|Al-Shaair before the 2018 FAU season.]]
Al-Shaair was a four-year starter at linebacker for the [[Florida Atlantic Owls football|Florida Atlantic Owls]]. As a freshman, Al-Shaair was named to the [[Conference USA]] All-Freshman team and named a Freshman All-American after recording a team-leading 94 tackles (7.5 for loss), 1.5 sacks, two passes broken up and a forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 12, 2015 |title=Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair Named USA Today Freshman All-American |url=https://fausports.com/news/2015/12/12/Linebacker_Azeez_Al_Shaair_Named_USA_Today_Freshman_All_American.aspx |access-date=September 2, 2019 |website=FAUSports.com}}</ref> He again led the Owls in tackles as a sophomore with 113 tackles (12 for loss), and returned an interception for a touchdown and was named as an honorable mention All-Conference USA.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DeFranks |first=Matthew |date=August 29, 2017 |title=FAU breakdown: players to watch, keys to season, crucial games |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/fl-sp-fau-playbook-20170808-story.html |access-date=September 2, 2019 |work=[[New York Daily News]] |publisher=[[Sun-Sentinel]]}}</ref> As a junior, Al-Shaair led Conference USA with 147 tackles (11 for loss) along with 2.5 sacks, four passes defensed and a forced fumble and was named first-team all conference. He entered his senior year on the [[Butkus Award]] watchlist but tore his ACL in a practice in October, ending his final season with just six games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Elman |first=Jake |date=July 23, 2018 |title=Florida Atlantic linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair named to Butkus Award watch list |url=http://faufocus.blog.palmbeachpost.com/2018/07/23/florida-atlantic-linebacker-azeez-al-shaair-named-to-butkus-award-watch-list/ |access-date=September 2, 2019 |work=[[Palm Beach Post]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Furones |first=David |date=October 18, 2018 |title=FAU linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair has senior season cut short due to torn ACL |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/fau-owls/fl-sp-fau-azeez-al-shaair-out-for-season-20181018-story.html |access-date=September 2, 2019 |work=[[Sun-Sentinel]]}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
Al-Shaair was signed by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on April 27, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Elman |first=Jake |date=April 27, 2019 |title=2019 NFL Draft: Florida Atlantic linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair signs with San Francisco 49ers as undrafted free agent |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/sports/20190427/2019-nfl-draft-florida-atlantic-linebacker-azeez-al-shaair-signs-with-san-francisco-49ers-as-undrafted-free-agent |access-date=September 2, 2019 |work=[[Palm Beach Post]]}}</ref> Al-Shaair made his NFL debut in the season-opener against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], playing exclusively on special teams and making two tackles in the 31-17 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hutchison |first=Jacob |date=September 9, 2019 |title=49ers snap count and position grades for Week 1 win over Bucs |url=http://www.knbr.com/2019/09/09/49ers-snap-count-and-position-grades-for-week-1-win-over-bucs/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190914045616/http://www.knbr.com/2019/09/09/49ers-snap-count-and-position-grades-for-week-1-win-over-bucs/ |archive-date=September 14, 2019 |access-date=September 18, 2019 |website=[[KNBR (AM)|KNBR.com]]}}</ref> The 49ers reached [[Super Bowl LIV]], but lost to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] by a score of 31–20.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LIV - San Francisco 49ers vs. Kansas City Chiefs - February 2nd, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202002020kan.htm |access-date=October 5, 2020 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He did not appear in any postseason games. Al-Shaair played in 15 games with four starts as a rookie, making 18 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Azeez Al-Shaair 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AlShAz00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=February 2, 2023 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

In Week 4 against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] on ''Sunday Night Football'' in 2020, Al-Shaair recorded his first career interception off a pass thrown by [[Carson Wentz]] during the 25–20 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at San Francisco 49ers - October 4th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010040sfo.htm |access-date=October 6, 2020 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

Al-Shaair entered the 2021 season as a starting linebacker for the 49ers. He started 13 games, finishing second on the team with 102 tackles, along with two sacks, five passes defensed, an interception, a forced fumble and two fumble recoveries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Azeez Al-Shaair 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AlShAz00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=February 2, 2023 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

On March 15, 2022, the 49ers placed a second-round restricted free agent tender on Al-Shaair.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Posey |first=Kyle |date=March 15, 2022 |title=NFL rumors tracker: 49ers give Azeez Al-Shaair a second-round tender, 1-year offer for $3.98 million |url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2022/3/15/22979140/49ers-rumors-contract-dee-ford-restructure-free-agency |access-date=February 1, 2023 |work=Niners Nation}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve with an [[medial collateral ligament|MCL]] sprain on October 3, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 3, 2022 |title=49ers Promote Willie Snead IV; Place Azeez Al-Shaair on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-promote-willie-snead-iv-place-azeez-al-shaair-on-injured-reserve |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=49ers.com}}</ref> He was activated on November 12.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 12, 2022 |title=49ers Activate Four Players From Injured Reserve; Place Verrett on IR |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-activate-four-players-from-injured-reserve-place-verrett-on-ir |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=49ers.com}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On March 20, 2023, Al-Shaair signed a one-year contract with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=March 20, 2023 |title=Titans Agree to Terms With Former 49ers LB Azeez Al-Shaair |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-agree-to-terms-with-former-49ers-lb-azeez-al-shaair |access-date=October 4, 2023 |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref> He started all 17 games and finished fifth in the league with 163 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Azeez Al-Shaair 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AlShAz00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-06-09 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL Defense |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2023/defense.htm |access-date=2024-06-09 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
[[File:Captains for Titans at Texans NOV2024.png|thumb|right|250px|Al-Shaair (#0) with the Houston Texans in 2024.]]
On March 15, 2024, Al-Shaair signed a three-year, $34 million contract with the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 15, 2024 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (03-15-2024) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-03-15-2024 |access-date=2024-07-11 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> Following Week 3, he was fined $11,000 for punching [[Chicago Bears]] running back, [[Roschon Johnson]], despite Al-Shaair not being ejected from the game.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/report-azeez-al-shaair-fined-11-000-for-punching-roschon-johnson|website=NBCSports.com|first=Charean|last=Williams|title=Report: Azeez Al-Shaair fined $11,000 for punching Roschon Johnson|date=September 19, 2024|accessdate=December 4, 2024}}</ref> He was issued a second fine for $11,255 after a late hit out of bounds on [[Tennessee Titans]] running back, [[Tony Pollard]].<ref name="Guardian apology">{{cite web|date=2024-12-02|title=Al-Shaair apologizes to Lawrence after illegal hit on defenseless quarterback|work=[[The Guardian]]|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2024/dec/02/al-shaair-apologizes-to-lawrence-after-hit-on-defenseless-quarterback|access-date=2024-12-02}}</ref> 

On December 1, 2024, Al-Shaair delivered an illegal hit to [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] quarterback, [[Trevor Lawrence]], after the latter had slid.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lewis |first=Juston |date=December 1, 2024 |title=Trevor Lawrence knocked out of game vs. Texans on dirty hit; Jaguars-Texans fight |url=https://www.jacksonville.com/story/sports/nfl/jaguars/2024/12/01/trevor-lawrence-hit-jacksonville-jaguars-houston-texans-fight/76689952007/ |access-date=2024-12-01 |work=The Florida Times-Union}}</ref> Lawrence was ruled out for the rest of the game with a concussion and Al-Shaair was ejected. A fight erupted between Al-Shaair and several Jaguar players, with Jacksonville cornerback, [[Jarrian Jones]], also getting ejected.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Joseph |first=Andrew |date=2024-12-01 |title=NFL fans were furious after Texans LB Aziz Al-Shaair's dangerous cheap shot on Trevor Lawrence |url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2024/12/texans-lb-aziz-al-shaair-ejected-trevor-lawrence-hit |access-date=2024-12-01 |work=For The Win |publisher=USA Today}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rapp |first=Timothy |date=December 1, 2024 |title=Video: Azeez Al-Shaair, Jarrian Jones Ejected; Trevor Lawrence Injured on Illegal Hit |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10145405-video-azeez-al-shaair-jarrian-jones-ejected-trevor-lawrence-injured-on-illegal-hit |access-date=2024-12-01 |work=Bleacher Report}}</ref> Al-Shaair publicly apologized via social media for the hit the next day.<ref name="Guardian apology"/> Two days after the game, Al-Shaair was suspended for three games with [[Jon Runyan]], the NFL's Vice President of the Policy and Rules, writing in the suspension letter that Al-Shaair's "continued disregard for NFL playing rules puts the health and safety of both [him] and [his] opponents in jeopardy and will not be tolerated."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Simmons |first1=Myles |title=Azeez Al-Shaair suspended for three games |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/azeez-al-shaair-suspended-for-three-games |access-date=3 December 2024 |work=NBC Sports |date=3 December 2024}}</ref>

In 2025, Al-Shaair led the Texans in tackles while anchoring one of the NFL’s top ranked defense, a performance that culminated in his first career selection to the Pro Bowl squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bodunrin |first=Ajibola |date=December 23, 2025 |title=Four Texans selected to 2026 Pro Bowl; three named starters |url=https://www.fox26houston.com/news/four-texans-selected-2026-pro-bowl-three-named-starters |access-date=December 25, 2025 |work=FOX 26 Houston}}</ref>

On April 29, 2026, the Texans signed Al-Shaair to a three-year, $54 million contract extension through the 2029 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sources: Texans, Azeez Al-Shaair agree to 3-year, $54M extension|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48628975/texans-lb-azeez-al-shaair-agree-3-year-extension|author=Bien-Aime, DJ|website=ESPN.com|date=April 29, 2026|access-date=May 2, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=HOUSTON TEXANS SIGN PRO BOWL LB AZEEZ AL-SHAAIR TO EXTENSION|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-sign-lb-azeez-al-shaair|website=houstontexans.com|date=May 1, 2026|access-date=May 4, 2026}}</ref>
