==Personal life==
Al-Shaair is a practicing Muslim and fasts during [[Ramadan]], including when he was participating in FAU's summer practices.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reynolds |first=Tim |date=August 27, 2018 |title=High hopes: FAU star LB Azeez Al-Shaair has overcome plenty |url=https://apnews.com/a0a9589108e9496099fd056058f3d82b |access-date=September 2, 2019 |website=[[Associated Press|APNews.com]]}}</ref> Al-Shaair has been deeply involved in community outreach and charitable work, partnering with organizations such as [[United Way]] and [[Covenant House]] to support underserved populations and homeless youth. He has also participated in the Texans Community Huddle Ticket Program, which provides game tickets and opportunities to engage with the players to students from disadvantaged communities. His service efforts have additionally included youth development initiatives, recognition of local firefighters, and humanitarian awareness related to [[Palestine]]. In recognition of his off-the-field leadership and impact, Al-Shaair was named the Texans’ nominee for the NFL’s [[Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year|Walter Payton Man of the Year Award]] for 2025.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Shapiro |first=Michael |title=Texans star uses 'Free Palestine' cleats to support voiceless |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/texans/article/texans-azeez-al-shaair-palestine-cleats-19894893.php |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20250605022329/https://www.chron.com/sports/texans/article/texans-azeez-al-shaair-palestine-cleats-19894893.php |archive-date=2025-06-05 |access-date=2025-12-12 |work=Chron}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL.com {{!}} Official Site of the National Football League |url=https://www.nfl.com/honors/man-of-the-year/nominees/2025/texans |access-date=December 25, 2025 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2025 |title=Controversial linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair earns recognition for all the right reasons |url=https://torotimes.com/controversial-linebacker-azeez-al-shaair-earns-recognition-for-all-the-right-reasons |access-date=December 25, 2025 |work=Toro Times}}</ref> 

Al-Shaair is an advocate for Palestinian rights and wore an [[eye black]] with the message "stop the [[Gaza genocide|genocide]]" during a post-game interview with ESPN on January 12, 2026 after the Texans' playoff win over the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Houston Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair wears ‘stop the genocide’ eye black|url=https://www.jpost.com/diaspora/antisemitism/article-883288|last=Strauss|first=Joseph|publisher=[[The Jerusalem Post]]|quote=But on the Pro Bowler’s eye black was a message that you don’t see every day on ESPN: “STOP THE GENOCIDE.” Al-Shaair, who is Muslim, has long been a vocal pro-Palestinian advocate.|date=January 14, 2026|accessdate=January 14, 2026}}</ref> Al-Shaair was fined $11,593 by the NFL for "violation of the NFL uniform and equipment rules." <ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/nfl-fines-texans-lb-azeez-al-shaair-11k-for-stop-the-genocide-eye-black/|title=NFL fines Texans LB Azeez Al-Shaair $11K for 'stop the genocide' message in eye black |author=Carter Bahns |date=January 18, 2026|work=CBS|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260118224244/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/nfl-fines-texans-lb-azeez-al-shaair-11k-for-stop-the-genocide-eye-black/|archive-date=January 18, 2026}}</ref> Al-Shaair wore a similar eye black during the January 18 game against the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6981232/2026/01/18/texans-azeez-al-shaair-eye-black-patriots-genocide/|title=Texans’ Azeez Al-Shaair wears ‘stop the genocide’ eye black for second straight game|author=Alfonso, Denny|date=January 18, 2026|work=New York Times|url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260118235814/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6981232/2026/01/18/texans-azeez-al-shaair-eye-black-patriots-genocide/ |archive-date=January 18, 2026}}</ref>

'''Azeez O. Ojulari'''{{Audio|Azeez_Ojulari.wav|listen}} (born June 16, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]] and was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the second round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Ojulari was born on June 16, 2000, in [[Austell, Georgia]] to Yoruba parents, and attended [[Marietta High School (Georgia)|Marietta High School]] in [[Marietta, Georgia]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sentell |first=Jeff |date=August 17, 2017 |title=BREAKING: Nation's No. 3 DE Azeez Ojulari chooses Georgia |url=https://www.dawgnation.com/football/recruiting/azeez-ojulari-2018-recruiting-commitment-georgia-bulldogs |access-date=April 7, 2021 |website=DawgNation.com}}</ref> As a senior, he had 118 tackles and 11 sacks before suffering a [[torn ACL]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moore |first=Maghen |date=December 17, 2017 |title=Justin Fields, other Georgia commits visit Azeez Ojulari after surgery |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/justin-fields-other-georgia-commits-visit-azeez-ojulari/HKF6KI3FVIqilwvitnIgIO/ |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution}}</ref> He was selected to the 2018 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]]. He committed to the [[University of Georgia]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=White |first=Carlton D. |date=August 17, 2017 |title=Marietta defensive end Azeez Ojulari commits to play at Georgia |url=https://www.mdjonline.com/cobb_football_friday/marietta-defensive-end-azeez-ojulari-commits-to-play-at-georgia/article_2d1e0ffe-83a8-11e7-8368-9bf89d4d2622.html |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=MDJOnline.com}}</ref>

==College career==
After recovering from the torn ACL he suffered his senior season of high school, Ojulari played in two games his first year at Georgia in 2018 and took a redshirt.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Paschall |first=David |date=August 12, 2019 |title=Azeez Ojulari among Georgia's promising outside linebackers |url=https://www.timesfreepress.com/news/2019/aug/12/azeez-ojulari-among-georgias-promising-outsid/ |access-date=February 6, 2023 |website=Chattanooga Times Free Press |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dennis |first=Ryne |date=September 4, 2019 |title=Back from torn ACL, Azeez Ojulari now major factor for Bulldogs |url=https://www.onlineathens.com/sports/20190904/back-from-torn-acl-azeez-ojulari-now-major-factor-for-bulldogs |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=Athens Banner-Herald}}</ref> As a redshirt freshman in 2019, he played in all 14 games and made 13 starts. He recorded 36 tackles and 5.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Leo |first=Jack |date=August 18, 2020 |title=Former Marietta standout Azeez Ojulari excited about another stout Georgia Bulldogs defense |url=https://www.mdjonline.com/sports/former-marietta-standout-azeez-ojulari-excited-about-another-stout-georgia-bulldogs-defense/article_fb25cd6c-b95f-553a-8ac1-4d4024ff6750.html |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=MDJOnline.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Leo |first=Jack |date=August 18, 2020 |title=Azeez Ojulari, Nakobe Dean excited about another stout Georgia Bulldogs defense |url=https://www.gwinnettdailypost.com/sports/azeez-ojulari-nakobe-dean-excited-about-another-stout-georgia-bulldogs-defense/article_77e681a2-e1be-11ea-9533-3b0a41f64bc8.html |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=Gwinnett Daily Post}}</ref> Ojulari returned to Georgia in 2020 as a starter.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Bailey |date=October 22, 2020 |title=Georgia's Azeez Ojulari becoming a force at pressuring a quarterback |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/georgia-bulldogs/georgias-azeez-ojulari-becoming-a-force-at-pressuring-a-quarterback/VYEJ4F56MRBWFFL5HHVXSKEUP4/ |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Towers |first=Chip |date=October 12, 2020 |title=Finally, a little recognition for Georgia's Azeez Ojulari |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/georgia-bulldogs/finally-a-little-recognition-for-georgias-azeez-ojulari/2R33NWLQMVC4LIRW2HT5Y7YJFA/ |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution}}</ref> During the 2020 season Ojulari was named second-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-SEC]] and was the defensive MVP of the [[2021 Peach Bowl (January)|2021 Peach Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Azeez Ojulari - 2020 - Football |url=https://georgiadogs.com/sports/football/roster/azeez-ojulari/4749 |access-date=May 1, 2021 |website=University of Georgia Athletics |language=en}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
Ojulari was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the second round (50th overall) of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schwartz |first=Paul |date=April 30, 2021 |title=Giants score potential NFL Draft coup with Azeez Ojulari pick |url=https://nypost.com/2021/04/30/2021-nfl-draft-giants-go-big-with-pass-rusher-azeez-ojulari/ |access-date=May 1, 2021 |website=New York Post}}</ref> He signed his four-year rookie contract on May 13, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Traina |first=Patricia |date=May 13, 2021 |title=Giants Sign Three Draft Picks |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/giants/gm-report/giants-sign-three-draft-picks |access-date=July 26, 2021 |website=SI.com}}</ref> Ojulari finished the season with 8 sacks which set an all-time Giants record for sacks by a rookie, surpassing [[B. J. Hill (American football)|B. J. Hill]], who recorded 5.5 sacks in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Benton |first=Dan |date=January 1, 2022 |title=Azeez Ojulari nearing Lawrence Taylor's unofficial Giants rookie sack record |url=https://giantswire.usatoday.com/2022/01/01/azeez-ojulari-nearing-lawrence-taylor-unofficial-new-york-giants-rookie-sack-record/ |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=Giants Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

On October 22, 2022, Ojulari was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salomone |first=Dan |date=October 22, 2022 |title=Landon Collins activated, Azeez Ojulari to IR among series of roster moves |url=https://www.giants.com/news/landon-collins-azeez-ojulari-ryder-anderson-quincy-roche0 |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> On December 3, he was activated from injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=December 3, 2022 |title=OLB Azeez Ojulari activated among series of moves |url=https://www.giants.com/news/azeez-ojulari-nick-vannett-ohio-state-buckeyes-tony-jefferson-roster |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> He finished the 2022 season with 5.5 sacks, ending the season second on the team behind nose tackle [[Dexter Lawrence]] in sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Azeez Ojulari 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OjulAz00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2023-08-20 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 New York Giants Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nyg/2022.htm |access-date=2023-08-20 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On October 14, 2023, Ojulari was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Azeez Ojulari to IR among series of roster moves|url=https://www.giants.com/news/azeez-ojulari-injured-reserve-justin-pugh-tommy-devito-jalen-mayfield-week-6|website=Giants.com|date=October 15, 2023}}</ref> On November 11, the Giants reactivated him back on their active roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.giants.com/news/azeez-ojulari-randy-bullock-tyree-jackson-dallas-cowboys-week-10-roster-moves|work=Giants.com|title=Giants activate OLB Azeez Ojulari from injured reserve|date=November 11, 2023|accessdate=November 11, 2023|first=Michael|last=Eisen}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On March 19, 2025, the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] signed Ojulari to a one-year deal worth $4 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles, Azeez Ojulari agree to terms on one-year deal|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-azeez-ojulari-agree-to-terms|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=March 17, 2025}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on November 1, due to a hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Eagles place S Marcus Epps, OLB Azeez Ojulari on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-place-marcus-epps-azeez-ojulari-on-injured-reserve|access-date=November 2, 2025|website=philadelphiaeagles.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On March 11, 2026, the [[Atlanta Falcons]] signed Ojulari to a one-year, $1.4 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlanta Falcons sign DE Azeez Ojulari|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/atlanta-falcons-sign-azeez-ojulari-georgia-bulldogs|author=McFadden, Will|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=March 16, 2026}}</ref>

'''Avery Williams''' (born July 15, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] and [[return specialist]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State Broncos]].

==Early life==
Williams was born to [[Pam Veasey]] and Marvin Williams on July 15, 1998. He is of Mexican descent through a grandmother.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 9, 2022 |title=NFL y la herencia mexicana |url=https://www.espn.com.mx/futbol-americano/nota/_/id/11049910/nfl-y-la-herencia-mexicana |website=ESPN.com.mx}}</ref> He grew up in [[Pasadena, California]] and originally attended [[Saint Francis High School (La Cañada Flintridge, California)|Saint Francis High School]] before transferring to [[JSerra Catholic High School]] before his senior year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Turner |first=Andrew |date=September 12, 2015 |title=Williams helps JSerra keep moving |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2015/09/12/williams-helps-jserra-keep-moving/ |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=[[Orange County Register]]}}</ref> As a senior, Williams was named [[Trinity League]] co-Most Valuable Player after rushing for 1,175 yards and 14 touchdowns on offense at running back and was also an All-Area selection at defensive back. He received no scholarship offers to play [[college football]] and enrolled at Boise State after being offered to join the team as a preferred walk-on.<ref name="Everything">{{Cite web |last=Rains |first=B.J. |date=September 12, 2018 |title=BOISE STATE GAVE AVERY WILLIAMS A CHANCE. NOW HE'S TRYING TO "GIVE THEM EVERYTHING I'VE GOT" IN RETURN |url=https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/football/boise-state-gave-avery-williams-a-chance-now-he-s/article_0f2cfb83-eee5-55ee-9fe7-b6d265b7003f.html |access-date=December 7, 2021 |website=[[The Idaho Press-Tribune]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Williams joined Boise State's football team as a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] and [[redshirted]] his true freshman season. He was named the Special Teams Scout Team Player of the Year during his redshirt year and awarded a scholarship during fall preseason training camp in 2017.<ref name=Everything/> Williams became the team's punt and kick returner as well as a starter at cornerback during his redshirt freshman season and finished the season with two interceptions and eight passes broken up and also returned two punts for touchdowns and was named second-team All-[[Mountain West Conference]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 8, 2017 |title=How Boise State football landed returner Avery Williams |url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-football/article172145642.html |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=[[Idaho Statesman]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 15, 2019 |title=Avery Williams is Boise State's spark on special teams |url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-football/article238375883.html |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=[[Idaho Statesman]]}}</ref>

As a redshirt sophomore, Williams recorded 49 tackles with 11 passes defended, two interceptions and three forced fumbles and returned a kickoff for a touchdown and was named honorable mention All-Mountain West.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 20, 2019 |title=Avery Williams is No. 3 on our list of Boise State's most important players |url=https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/football/avery-williams-is-no-3-on-our-list-of-boise-states-most-important-players-in/article_97f2297b-bd80-530a-87a7-b0fc60753bac.html |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=[[Idaho Statesman]]}}</ref> He was again named honorable mention All-Mountain West after recording 39 tackles with four passes broken up and returning 22 punts for 290 yards and two touchdowns in his junior season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 7, 2020 |title=Offseason Outlook: Williams looking to rebound at cornerback |url=https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/football/offseason-outlook-williams-looking-to-rebound-at-cornerback-for-boise-state/article_863aeefc-a9f4-5c9d-89c7-4d431da8c118.html |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=[[The Idaho Press-Tribune]]}}</ref> As a senior, Williams returned 19 kickoffs for 533 yards and two touchdowns and 15 punts for 229 yards and two touchdowns, tying the [[NCAA Division I]] career record with nine return touchdowns. He was named first-team All-Mountain West and the Conference Special Teams Player of the Year as a returner and was a consensus first-team [[All-American]] selection as an all-purpose player.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 30, 2020 |title=College football's top senior student-athlete plays at Boise State; Williams honored again |url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-football/article248177270.html |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=[[Idaho Statesman]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 31, 2020 |title=Avery Williams becomes Boise State's first consensus All-American in 9 years |url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-football/article248201730.html |website=[[Idaho Statesman]]}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
Williams was selected by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in the fifth round (183rd overall) of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Falcons select CB Avery Williams in fifth round of NFL Draft |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-select-cb-avery-williams-in-fifth-round-of-nfl-draft |access-date=May 2, 2021 |website=Atlanta Falcons}}</ref> He signed his four-year rookie contract with Atlanta on June 15, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 15, 2021 |title=Falcons Sign Five Draft Picks |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2021/06/falcons-sign-five-draft-picks-2 |website=Pro Football Rumors}}</ref> He was the Falcons primary kick and punt returner as well as a core special teamer and gunner in 2021.

In the 2022 offseason, the Falcons moved Williams to running back, going back to his primary position in high school.<ref name="b859">{{cite web | last=McElhaney | first=Tori | title=Falcons move Avery Williams to new position | website=Atlanta Falcons | date=May 26, 2022 | url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-move-avery-williams-to-new-position | access-date=December 31, 2024}}</ref>

On June 7, 2023, head coach [[Arthur Smith (American football, born 1982)|Arthur Smith]] announced that Williams tore his [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] while participating in the Falcons' [[organized team activities]] (OTAs) and would miss the entire season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |date=June 7, 2023 |title=Falcons' Avery Williams likely to miss season after ACL tear |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/37812932/falcons-avery-williams-likely-miss-season-acl-tear |access-date=June 8, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on June 16.<ref name="e984">{{cite web | last=Simmons | first=Myles | title=Falcons sign three minicamp tryout players | website=NBC Sports | date=June 16, 2023 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/falcons-sign-three-minicamp-tryout-players | access-date=December 19, 2024}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On March 15, 2025, Williams signed a one-year contract with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 15, 2025 |title=Eagles, Avery Williams agree to terms on one-year deal |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-avery-williams-agree-to-terms |access-date=21 March 2025 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> He was released on August 26 as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Eagles announce their initial 53-man roster |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-announce-initial-53-man-roster-2025-season |website=philadelphiaeagles.com |access-date=27 August 2025}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
On October 3, 2025, Williams signed with the [[New York Jets]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Weir |first1=Susanna |title=Jets Sign RB Avery Williams to Practice Squad |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-avery-williams-practice-squad-release-lawrence-toafili-10-03-2025 |website=newyorkjets.com |access-date=4 October 2025}}</ref> He was released on October 14.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Weir |first1=Susanna |title=Jets Release DL Leonard Taylor III |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-release-leonard-taylor-sign-wr-trenton-irwin-to-practice-squad-10-14-2025 |website=newyorkjets.com |access-date=15 October 2025}}</ref>

'''Auzoyah Alufohai''' (born October 16, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[nose tackle]]. After playing [[college football]] for the [[West Georgia Wolves football|West Georgia Wolves]], he signed with the [[Houston Texans]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2020.

==Professional career==
===Houston Texans===
Alufohai signed with the [[Houston Texans]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] following the [[2020 NFL draft]] on April 27, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Transactions: Texans sign two free agents, nine college free agents |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/transactions-texans-sign-two-free-agents-nine-college-free-agents |website=HoustonTexans.com |date=April 27, 2020 |access-date=February 4, 2021}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts on September 5, 2020,<ref>{{cite news |title=Transactions: Roster Moves (9-5-2020) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/transactions-roster-moves-9-5-2020 |website=HoustonTexans.com |date=September 5, 2020 |access-date=February 4, 2021}}</ref> and signed to the team's [[practice squad]] two days later.<ref>{{cite news |title=Texans Announce Roster Moves (9-7-2020) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-announce-roster-moves-x3423 |website=HoustonTexans.com |date=September 7, 2020 |access-date=February 4, 2021}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on December 19 for the team's week 15 game against the [[Indianapolis Colts]], and reverted to the practice squad after the game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Houston Texans Transactions (12-19-20) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-12-19-20 |website=HoustonTexans.com |date=December 19, 2020 |access-date=February 4, 2021}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 23, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Houston Texans Transactions (12-23-20) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-12-23-20-x6653 |website=HoustonTexans.com |date=December 23, 2020 |access-date=February 4, 2021}}</ref>

On August 24, 2021, Alufohai was waived by the Texans.

===Chicago Bears===
On September 1, 2021, Alufohai was signed to the [[Chicago Bears]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears sign 13 players to practice squad|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-sign-13-players-to-practice-squad|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=September 1, 2021}}</ref> He was released on September 8, 2021.

===Green Bay Packers===
On November 3, 2021, Alufohai was signed to the [[Green Bay Packers]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Packers place QB Aaron Rodgers on reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-place-qb-aaron-rodgers-on-reserve-covid-19-list |publisher=packers.com |access-date=November 3, 2021}}</ref> He was released on November 16, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers place LB Whitney Mercilus on injured reserve|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-place-lb-whitney-mercilus-on-injured-reserve|website=Packers.com|date=November 16, 2021|access-date=November 17, 2021|archive-date=November 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211116224101/https://www.packers.com/news/packers-place-lb-whitney-mercilus-on-injured-reserve|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears (second stint)===
On December 16, 2021, Alufohai was signed to the Bears practice squad. He signed a reserve/future contract with the Bears on January 11, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Bears sign 11 to reserve/future contracts|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-sign-11-to-reserve-future-contracts|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=January 11, 2022}}</ref> He was waived on August 5, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer, Larry |date=August 5, 2022 |title=Roster Moves: Bears sign DL Coley, CB Harris |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-move-bears-sign-dl-coley-cb-harris |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On August 10, 2022, Alufohai signed with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 10, 2022 |title=Roster Moves: The Jaguars sign DL Auzoyah Alufohai and waive Jeremiah Ledbetter |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-the-jaguars-sign-dl-auzoyah-alufohai-and-waive-jeremiah-ledbetter |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> He was waived on August 29, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Jaguars release four, waive six ahead of the 53-man roster deadline on August 30, 2022|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-jaguars-release-four-waive-six-ahead-of-the-53-man-deadline-on-augu|website=Jaguars.com|date=August 29, 2022}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Stars===
Alufohai signed with the [[Philadelphia Stars (2022)|Philadelphia Stars]] of the [[United States Football League (2022)|United States Football League]] (USFL) on August 11, 2023.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLStars |title=Free Agent Signing |number=1690176431278678016 |date=August 11, 2023 |access-date=August 11, 2023}}</ref> The Stars folded when the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]] and USFL merged to create the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seifert |first=Kevin |date=January 1, 2024 |title=Newly formed United Football League sets 8 markets, tabs coaches |url=https://www.espn.com/xfl/story/_/id/39222541/newly-formed-united-football-league-sets-8-markets-tabs-coaches |access-date=January 15, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

'''Azur Kamara''' (born September 26, 1998) is an Ivorian professional [[gridiron football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Kansas Jayhawks football|Kansas]]. He signed with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] as an undrafted free agent. He has also been a member of the [[Carolina Panthers]], [[Kansas City Chiefs]], and [[Edmonton Elks]].

==Early life==
Kamara was born in [[Abidjan]], [[Ivory Coast]]. He moved to the [[United States]] at the age of 10, after his mother finally gained approval to send for her four children (there was a maximum of three children allowed). His mother had arrived 5 years earlier as a refugee from the [[First Ivorian Civil War]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://sports.yahoo.com/from-refugee-to-nfl-draft-azur-kamara-cherishes-a-remarkable-journey-160858574.html | title=From refugee to NFL draft, Azur Kamara cherishes a remarkable journey | access-date=September 2, 2021}}</ref>

He attended [[Central High School (Phoenix, Arizona)|Central High School]]. As a freshman, he began playing [[American football]] for the first time.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.texasmonthly.com/arts-entertainment/azur-kamara-cowboys/ | title=Azur Kamara’s Feel-good Path From West Africa to the Dallas Cowboys | access-date=September 2, 2021}}</ref> As a senior, he had 106 tackles, 25.5 sacks, 4 forced fumbles and one fumble recovery, while receiving All-conference honors.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://m.kusports.com/news/2018/sep/18/tom-keegan-azura-kamara-grateful-journey-african-s/ | title=Tom Keegan: Azur Kamara grateful for journey from African soccer player to Kansas football player | access-date=September 2, 2021}}</ref>

==College career==
===Arizona Western===
Kamara enrolled at [[Arizona Western College]]. As a freshman, he tallied 45 tackles, 13.5 tackles-for-loss, 8 sacks, 4 forced fumbles and 2 fumble recoveries.

As a sophomore, he posted 30 tackles, 15.5 tackles-for-loss (led the team), 12.5 sacks, 3 forced fumbles, one pass breakup and one blocked kick, while contributing to the team reaching the [[NJCAA]] national title game.

===Kansas===
He transferred to the [[University of Kansas]] after his sophomore season. As a junior, he appeared in all 12 games with 3 starts. He registered 16 tackles (5 for loss), one sack, one quarterback hurry, one pass breakup and one forced fumble.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://kuathletics.com/azur-kamara-reflects-on-journey-leading-up-to-the-nfl-draft/ | title=Azur Kamara Reflects on Journey Leading up to the NFL Draft | access-date=September 2, 2021}}</ref>

As a senior, he was named the starter at [[outside linebacker]]. He started 12 games, while making 51 tackles (sixth on the team), 6 tackles-for-loss (second on the team), 3.5 sacks and 4 quarterback hurries.

Kamara played with fellow Jayhawk [[Hakeem Adeniji]] in the [[2020 Senior Bowl]].

'''Jamiu Bolaji''' "'''BJ'''" '''Ojulari'''{{audio|LL-Q34311 (yor)-Abike25-Jamiu Bolaji "BJ" Ojulari.wav|listen}}(born April 5, 2002) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]].

==Early life==
Ojulari grew up in [[Marietta, Georgia]], and attended [[Marietta High School (Georgia)|Marietta High School]]. As a senior, he set a school record with 19 sacks and was named the Area Defensive Player of the Year with ''[[Marietta Daily Journal]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mdjonline.com/cobb_football_friday/mdj-defensive-player-of-the-year-ojulari-leads-marietta-defense-to-new-heights/article_a0ef303e-259a-11ea-8dc2-df03671464c5.html|title=MDJ Defensive Player of the Year: Ojulari leads Marietta defense to new heights|first=John|last=Bednarowski|work=[[Marietta Daily Journal]]|date=December 25, 2019|access-date=September 23, 2021}}</ref> Ojulari initially committed to play [[college football]] at Tennessee, but flipped his commitment to LSU during senior season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Toppmeyer |first=Blake |date=October 27, 2019 |title=Four-star DE BJ Ojulari flips commitment from Tennessee to LSU |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/football/2019/10/27/tennessee-football-bj-ojulari-lsu-tigers-recruiting-rankings-commits-decommitment-ut-vols/2479430001/ |access-date=September 23, 2021 |website=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Ojulari played in all ten of LSU's games as a freshman and finished the season with 16 tackles, four sacks, and five tackles for loss with a forced fumble and a fumble recovery and was named to the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Freshman team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dixon |first=Shea |date=January 6, 2021 |title=BJ Ojulari returns in 2021 after Freshman All-SEC season |url=https://247sports.com/college/lsu/Article/LSU-Tigers-football-defensive-end-BJ-Ojulari-will-return-in-2021-sophomore-year-158667856/ |access-date=June 6, 2023 |website=247Sports |language=en}}</ref> He was named the SEC Defensive Lineman of the Week after sacking [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina]] quarterback [[Collin Hill]] three times for a loss of 21 yards.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wafb.com/2020/10/26/lsu-de-bj-ojulari-kr-trey-palmer-named-sec-players-week/|title=LSU DE BJ Ojulari and KR Trey Palmer named SEC Players of the Week|first=Josh|last=Auzenne|website=[[WAFB|WAFB.com]]|date=October 26, 2020|access-date=September 23, 2021}}</ref> Ojulari was named the conference Defensive Lineman of the Week a second time after a 2½ sack performance in a 49-21 win over [[Central Michigan Chippewas football|Central Michigan]] in the third week of his sophomore season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_d5136948-1c8d-11ec-ad1b-8b85d41423ab.html|title=BJ the Beast: Ojulari using 'natural-born' pass-rushing skills to help LSU lead the nation in sacks|first=Sheldon|last=Mickles|work=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]]|date=September 23, 2021|access-date=September 23, 2021}}</ref>

Ojulari began the 2025 season on the reserve/PUP list while he recovered from his ACL injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bam Knight Surprise, Nolen On PUP As Cardinals Make Final Cuts To Get To 53-Man Roster|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-make-final-cuts-to-get-to-53-man-roster-bam-knight-walter-nolen-will-hernandez|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=August 26, 2025}}</ref> He was activated on November 15, 2025, ahead of the team's Week 11 matchup against the [[2025 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=BJ Ojulari Returns To Roster; Mack Wilson Sr. Heads To Injured Reserve|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/bj-ojulari-returns-to-roster-mack-wilson-sr-heads-to-injured-reserve|access-date=November 19, 2025|website=azcardinals.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ojulari's parents immigrated to the United States from Nigeria and his maternal grandfather was the [[Yoruba people|Yoruba]] artist [[Twins Seven Seven]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_85e3a092-fce3-11ea-b840-47ef20a1a83c.html|title=Meet LSU's B.J. Ojulari: grandson of a Nigerian prince, descendant of a king — and a key pass rusher|first=Brooks|last=Kubena|work=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]]|date=September 22, 2020|access-date=September 23, 2021}}</ref> His older brother, [[Azeez Ojulari]], played college football for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]] before being drafted by the [[New York Giants]] in the second round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2167271/2020/10/29/azeez-and-bj-ojulari-brothers-georgia-lsu-pass-rushers-sec/|title='For family': Behind what drives the SEC's Ojulari-brother pass-rush tandem|first1=Seth|last1=Emerson|first2=Brody|last2=Miller|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=October 29, 2020|access-date=September 23, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Schwartz |first=Paul |date=April 30, 2021 |title=Giants score potential NFL Draft coup with Azeez Ojulari pick |url=https://nypost.com/2021/04/30/2021-nfl-draft-giants-go-big-with-pass-rusher-azeez-ojulari/ |access-date=May 1, 2021 |website=New York Post}}</ref>

He finished his career with 142 receptions for 1,744 yards and 13 touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/falcons-austin-trammell-joins-atlanta/|title=Falcons' Austin Trammell: Joins Atlantar|website=[[CBSSports.com]]|publisher=[[RotoWire]]|date=May 4, 2021|access-date=January 3, 2022}}</ref>

On June 16, 2022, Trammell was released by the Falcons.<ref>{{cite web|title= Falcons sign offensive lineman, defensive lineman after minicamp tryout |url= https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-sign-offensive-lineman-defensive-lineman-after-minicamp-tryout |website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=June 16, 2022}}</ref>

'''Azareye'h Thomas''' (born July 6, 2004) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State Seminoles]] and was selected by the Jets in the third round of the [[2025 NFL draft]]. He is the younger brother of NFL player [[Juanyeh Thomas]].

== Early life ==
Thomas attended [[Niceville High School]] in [[Niceville, Florida]], where he was a two-way player on the [[high school football|football]] team.<ref>{{cite web | last=Greenberg | first=Ethan | title=Jets Select Florida State CB Azareye'h Thomas with the 73rd Overall Pick in the 2025 NFL Draft | website=New York Jets | date=2025-04-26 | url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/azareyeh-thomas-nfl-draft-cornerback-florida-state | access-date=2026-04-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Karels |first1=Carter |title=FSU football: Freshman Azareye'h Thomas off to hot start in preseason |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/football/2022/08/02/fsu-football-freshman-azareyeh-thomas-off-hot-start-preseason/10199402002/ |website=Tallahassee Democrat |date=2 August 2022 |access-date=20 August 2024}}</ref> He was rated as a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], where he also held offers from schools such as Florida, Florida State, Georgia Tech, LSU, and Oklahoma.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Patterson |first1=Chip |title=College football recruiting: Four-star athlete Azareyeh Thomas commits to Florida State over Florida, Georgia |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/college-football-recruiting-four-star-athlete-azareyeh-thomas-commits-to-florida-state-over-florida-georgia/ |website=CBS Sports |date=15 December 2021 |access-date=20 August 2024}}</ref> Ultimately, Thomas decided to commit to play [[college football]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State Seminoles]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fawcett |first1=Hayes |title=4-star S Azareye'h Thomas commits to Florida State Seminoles |url=https://www.on3.com/college/florida-state-seminoles/news/4-star-s-azareyeh-thomas-commits-to-florida-state-seminoles/ |website=On3.com |date=15 December 2021 |access-date=20 August 2024}}</ref>

== College career ==
In week 10 of the 2022 season, Thomas recorded his first career interception in a win over [[2022 Miami Hurricanes football team|Miami]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Bakich |first1=Jackson |title=FSU DB Azareye'h Thomas Picked To Be Breakout Player In 2024 |url=https://www.si.com/college/fsu/football/fsu-db-azareyeh-thomas-picked-breakout-player-2024 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=19 February 2024 |access-date=20 August 2024}}</ref> He finished his freshman season with 14 tackles with two being for a loss, a pass deflection, and an interception.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=Jack |title=Azareye'h Thomas taking a major, expected leap in early FSU football spring practices |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/football/2024/03/27/azareyeh-thomas-credits-mental-game-in-elevated-game-with-fsu-football/73089006007/ |website=Tallahassee Democrat |date=27 March 2024 |access-date=20 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Corey |title=CB Azareye'h Thomas ranks No. 3 on Florida State Top 40 |url=https://www.on3.com/teams/florida-state-seminoles/news/warchant-top-40-no-3-azareyeh-thomas-ready-to-take-over-starting-and-starring-role-for-fsu-defense/ |website=On3.com |date=5 July 2024 |access-date=20 August 2024}}</ref> In 2023, Thomas played all 14 games for the Seminoles where he notched 29 tackles with four and a half being for a loss, ten pass deflections, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Holland Jr. |first1=Peter |title=Florida State football's Fentrell Cypress II, Azareye'h Thomas may be nation's top CB duo |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/football/2024/07/31/florida-state-football-cornerbacks-top-duo-fentrell-cypress-azareyeh-thomas/74584994007/ |website=Tallahassee Democrat |date=31 July 2024 |access-date=20 August 2024}}</ref>

'''Avieon Terrell''' (born January 11, 2005) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] and was selected by the Falcons in the second round of the [[2026 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Terrell attended [[Westlake High School (Georgia)|Westlake High School]] in [[Atlanta, Georgia]]. He played cornerback and [[wide receiver]] in high school. During his career he had 86 tackles and six [[interceptions]]. He committed to [[Clemson University]] to play college football.<ref name="d867">{{cite web | last=Bezjak | first=Lou | title=Clemson football lands commitment from brother of former Tigers standout | website=The State | date=2022-06-06 | url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/acc/clemson-university/article262202837.html | access-date=2024-10-08}}</ref><ref name="nytimes">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4175661/2022/06/06/clemson-snags-pledge-from-4-star-cb-avieon-terrell/|title=Clemson snags pledge from 4-star CB Avieon Terrell|work=The New York Times |date=2022-06-06|access-date=2024-09-15 |last1=Raynor |first1=Grace }}</ref>

==College career==

'''Ayo Oyelola''' (born 19 October 1998) is an English professional [[gridiron football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

==Early life==
From [[East London]], Oyelola was a [[association football|soccer]] player in his youth, and featured in the academy at teams such as [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]], [[Dagenham and Redbridge F.C.|Dagenham and Redbridge]] and [[Ebbsfleet FC|Ebbsfleet]]. He started playing [[American football]] at the [[University of Nottingham]], where he graduated with a law degree in 2020.<ref name="jig">{{cite web|first=Cameron|last=Hogwood|date=10 October 2023|url=https://www.skysports.com/nfl/news/12118/12981689/ayo-oyelola-jacksonville-jaguars-safety-embraces-crisp-british-air-on-uk-homecoming|title= Ayo Oyelola: Jacksonville Jaguars safety embraces crisp British air on UK homecoming |accessdate=9 December 2024|website=Sky Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/currentstudents/news/uon-graduate-signed-by-national-football-league-nfl-team|website=Nottingham.ac.uk|accessdate=9 December 2024|title= UoN graduate signed by National Football League (NFL) team|date=13 May 2022}}</ref><ref name="peaxh">{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/nfl-jacksonville-jaguars-declan-rice-mason-mount-buffalo-bills-b2101819.html|website=Independent.co.uk|title= Ayo Oyelola: Ex-teammate of Mason Mount and Declan Rice with eyes on NFL career|accessdate=9 December 2024|first=Simon|last=Peach|date=15 June 2022}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Winnipeg Blue Bombers (first stint)===
Oyelola started out as a [[linebacker]] before transitioning to safety.<ref name="jig"/> He was drafted 22nd in the [[2021 CFL global draft]] by [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]].<ref>{{cite web|date=1 June 2021|url= https://www.americanfootballinternational.com/winnipeg-blue-bombers-sign-2021-cfl-global-draft-pick-ayo-oyelola/amp/|website=American Football International|accessdate=9 December 2024|title= Winnipeg Blue Bombers sign 2021 CFL Global Draft pick Ayo Oyelola}}</ref> Oyelola made his debut for the Winnipeg Blue Bombers in the [[Canadian Football League]] on 20 November 2021 against the [[Calgary Stampeders]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.americanfootballinternational.com/?p=137678#google_vignette|accessdate=9 December 2024|title= UK linebacker Ayo Oyelola makes CFL debut with the Winnipeg Blue Bombers|first= Alex |last=Malchow | website=American Football International |date=23 November 2021}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
In December 2020, it was announced that Oyelola had been one of eleven athletes from around to world to selected to participate in the [[NFL]] [[International Player Pathway]] (IPP).<ref name="jig"/> He did not secure a contract with an NFL team and decided to play in the CFL. In January 2022 it was announced that he was again selected to be a part of the NFL IPP, this time involving 13 athletes from around the world.<ref>{{cite web|website=Verge Magazine|accessdate=9 December 2024|url=https://vergemagazine.co.uk/nfl-three-british-players-make-the-ipp/|date=11 January 2022|title=NFL: THREE BRITISH PLAYERS MAKE THE IPP|first=Andre|last=Dixon}}</ref> He was signed by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] later that year.<ref name="peaxh"/> He was waived by the Jaguars on 30 August 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news4jax.com/sports/2022/08/30/jaguars-cuts-recent-draft-picks-jay-tufele-gregory-junior-among-teams-final-cuts/|website=news4jax.com|accessdate=9 December 2024|title= Jaguars cuts: Recent draft picks Jay Tufele, Gregory Junior among team's final cuts|first=Justin|last=Barney|date=30 August 2022}}</ref> Oyelola re-signed with Jacksonville's practice squad the next day and spent the remainder of the season on the practice squad.

On 23 January 2023, he signed a reserve/futures contract with the Jaguars, but was waived again on 29 August, the conclusion of training camp. He later re-signed to the team's practice squad, where he spent the remainder of the season. On 9 January 2024, Oyelola signed a reserve/futures contract with the Jaguars. He was waived on 15 April.

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On 2 September 2024, Oyelola was signed to a one year contract by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], and joined their practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers sign British DB Ayo Oyelola to practice squad|url=https://triblive.com/sports/steelers-sign-british-db-ayo-oyelola-to-practice-squad/ |website=Triblive|first=Chris|last=Adamski|date= 2 September 2024|accessdate=9 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://atozsports.com/nfl/pittsburgh-steelers-news/steelers-news-ipp-player-practice-squad-ayo-oyelola/|website=atozsports.com|accessdate=9 December 2024|title=Steelers finalize their roster by taking advantage of one of the NFL's smartest rules|first=Rob|last=Gregson|date=2 September 2024}}</ref> He was released on 11 January 2025.<ref name="db"/>

===Winnipeg Blue Bombers (second stint)===
Oyelola signed with the Blue Bombers' practice roster on September 3, 2025.<ref name="db"/> He was released on September 8, 2025.<ref name="db">{{cite web | url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/ayo-oyelola-oyeloay01/transactions | title=Ayo Oyelola | publisher=FootballDB.com | accessdate=12 June 2026}}</ref>

===Alpine Rams===
On March 27, 2026, Oyelola signed with the [[Alpine Rams]] of the [[American Football League Europe]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.aflepro.com/news/alpine-rams-sign-former-nfl-and-cfl-defensive-back-ayo-oyelola | title=Alpine Rams sign former NFL and CFL defensive back Ayo Oyelola | publisher=[[American Football League Europe]] | date=March 27, 2026 | accessdate=12 June 2026}}</ref>

===Winnipeg Blue Bombers (third stint)===
Oyelola was signed to the Blue Bombers' practice roster again on June 8, 2026.<ref name="db"/>
